concerns.recommendation: Fold into ONE surviving GEM row for the Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine system (КЗУ), and do NOT carry P0777's 1,112.00 km / 522+590 km figures onto it. Those rest on VTG (vtg.com.ua/experience/main/gts.html), which is a genuine 404 ('Сторінку не знайдено', confirmed live) — so they are unsourced, not merely unverified. The operator's own construction chronology, read through Wayback after this cluster was first adjudicated, gives the system as 183.6 km (1970, ∅1020) + 216.3 km (1972, ∅1220) = 399.90 km, which is exactly what P1480 already carries; use P1480's value on the surviving row whichever PID survives. P0777's diameters (1020/1220 mm) and StartYear1 (1970) are corroborated and can be kept. One thing for the human to decide rather than assume: the chronology calls the 1970 build the first stage of the CONTINUATION of the separate Yefremivka–Dolyna–Kyiv trunk, so 1,112 km may be a conflation of KЗУ with that upstream trunk rather than a simple error — if so the fix is a scope statement in ResearcherNotes, not just a smaller number. [main-loop correction 2026-08-16 — VTG is ARCHIVED, and the 522+590 reading is a grouped-cell misread] Two amendments, neither of which disturbs the verdict or the 399.90 km resolution. (1) The claim that P0777's figures are 'unsourced, not merely unverified' because vtg.com.ua 404s is WITHDRAWN. The live URL does 404, but a Wayback capture of the ВНІПІтрансгаз "Основные объекты" table verifies 200 and serves the full table: https://web.archive.org/web/20220608014635/http://www.vtg.com.ua/experience/main/gts.html?lang=ru . Standing practice in this repo is to REPOINT a ref to its archived capture, not to treat the content as unsourced; the figures are sourceable, they are simply misread (below). (2) The archived table CONFIRMS the conflation this recommendation had left for the human to decide. VTG groups four lines under one 'Система газопроводов' block with a rowspan'd name cell, and the sub-names map in order to the data rows: Шебелинка-Полтава-Київ = 700 mm / 438 km, Єфремівка-Диканька-Київ = 1000 mm / 477.8 km, Шебелинка-Диканька-Київ = 1000 mm / 522 km, and Київ-Захід України = 1000,1200 mm / 590 km, 1 нитка. So 522 and 590 are TWO DIFFERENT LINES: 1,112.00 km is the КЗУ line plus the upstream Shebelinka-Dykanka-Kyiv trunk added together. That is a documented conflation, not an unexplained number, so the fix is a scope statement in ResearcherNotes alongside the smaller value, exactly as this recommendation anticipated. (3) Note for whoever applies it: VTG's own КЗУ figure is 590 km on ONE string, against UTG's 183.6 + 216.3 = 399.90 km on two. The operator's construction chronology is the better source and 399.90 stands; record the 590 as a documented second-source tension rather than resolving it silently. Reading any single number off this table without checking its rowspan grouping is the trap — the same block structure puts three separate lines under 'Північний Кавказ-Центр'.

concerns.recommendation: Do NOT fold or delete yet — the duplicate question is genuinely unresolved on sourcing (see cluster notes). Independently, FIX the length field: 333.00 km is geometrically impossible for the stated endpoints. Ananiv (Odesa Oblast, ~47.73°N 30.00°E) to Bohorodchany (Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, ~48.80°N 24.51°E) are ~424 km apart on a great circle, so no pipeline route between them can be only 333 km; a pipe is always ≥ the straight-line distance between its own endpoints. Chase where '333' originated (it matches neither the 532.6 km whole-K-A-B-trunk figure nor Moldovatransgaz's own 184.8 km Moldovan-territory-portion figure for the same-named АЧБ trunk) — it looks like a transcription error or a conflation with an unrelated segment length, and should be corrected or the row's true extent re-examined regardless of how the duplicate question resolves. Next step to actually close the duplicate question: get a verbatim (non-WAF-blocked) copy of the Ukrtransgaz historical chronology (utg.ua) and the Bohorodchanske LVUMG chronology page (tsoua.com) — both 403 automated fetches and have no Wayback capture; try a different egress IP, a library/archival route, or ask GEM's Ukraine contacts directly. A single unstable, non-reproducing search-engine synthesis of the tsoua.com page claimed Ukrtransgaz's chronology names TWO separately-commissioned 1987-88 pipelines ('Kremenchuk-Ananiev-Chernivtsi' and 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany') distinct from the 1986 'Kremenchuk-Ananiev-Bohorodchany' — if that specific claim can be verified verbatim, it would REFUTE the duplicate hypothesis (parallel Soviet-era strings, same pattern as the Kazakhstan precedent). A repeat search on the same terms failed to reproduce that claim, so treat it as unconfirmed until read first-hand.
concerns.researcher_notes: [cluster C — UNRESOLVED: Anan'iv–Bohorodchany cluster (P1481 vs P1485): UNRESOLVED — genuine, well-sourced ambiguity between one trunk under two partial names and two independently built parallel lines] Structural hypothesis: P1481's own endpoints (Ananiv→Bohorodchany) are a literal subset of P1485's endpoints (Kremenchuk→Bohorodchany via Ananiv), same diameter (1020 mm both), similar capacity (9.10 vs 8.70 bcm/y). Moldovatransgaz's own asset registry (fetched verbatim, https://moldovatransgaz.md/... and mirror http://mtg.md/ru/news/54) lists as one of its 8 serviced magistral trunks: '1. Ананьев - Черновцы - Богородчаны (АЧБ) – газопровод, предназначенный для передачи природного газа потребителям Республики Молдова протяженностью 184,8 км, диаметром 1020 мм, с пропускной способностью 9,1 млрд м3 в год'. This confirms 'АЧБ' EXISTS as a distinctly named entity, matching P1481's name near-exactly and its capacity exactly (9.1), and diameter exactly (1020 mm). Separately, TTGPMR (Transnistria's own gas operator, ttgpmr.com/company/history/, institutionally independent of Moldovatransgaz) also names 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bogorodchany' verbatim ('Позже он был соединён 22-километровой перемычкой с газопроводом Ананьев-Черновцы-Богородчаны'), giving a THIRD, independent institutional confirmation the name is real — but none of these three sources states outright whether AChB is (a) the same physical pipe as P1485's western half, described under a Moldovan-side partial name, or (b) a separate parallel string built later in the same corridor. Working against distinctness: the dedicated Ukrainian Wikipedia article on 'Kremenchuk-Ananiv-Bohorodchany' already routes the SAME 532/532.6 km, 1986, 1020 mm trunk through Ananiv → Sholdănești (Moldova, commissioned 1988) → Drochia (Moldova) → Khotyn (Chernivtsi Oblast) → (implied) Bohorodchany — i.e. through the SAME corridor and even the same Chernivtsi-Oblast waypoint (Khotyn) that 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany' names, and when asked directly to check, the article was confirmed to contain NO mention of a second/parallel pipe or thread ('нитка'). That silence, from a dedicated single-pipeline article that otherwise lists individual compressor stations in detail, is meaningful (though not conclusive) evidence for ONE physical trunk under two partial, institution-specific names rather than two physical trunks.

Ділянка УТ-5 (км 55,1 - км 68,6)', customer PJSC Ukrtransgaz -- states the reconstruction covers the FULL corridor km1.1-68.0, length 67km, i.e. essentially P3381's whole route minus the first 1.1km. (2) Nashi Groshi, 04.12.2015: Ukrtransgaz's Kharkivtransgaz branch awarded a 95.85M UAH contract (30 Nov 2015) to TOV 'Trubremont' to build a new Du500 pipe PARALLEL to the existing Du700 route over the full 67km, then tie in to the operating system -- explicit replacement methodology, target completion end-2016. (3) ProZorro/openprocurement.org public API, tender UA-2020-04-01-000023-c, 'Section UT-4 (km39.9-55.1). RESIDUAL WORKS' -- procuring entity 'Operator of the Gas Transmission System of Ukraine' (TSOU), status complete, one active contract signed 21 May 2020 for 29,657,697.56 UAH gross. This 2020 'residual works' contract is direct evidence the project had NOT finished on the original 2015-2016 schedule and was still under construction 4+ years later. A companion UT-5 2020 construction tender (title indexed as UA-2020-06-10-007174-b) and a 2019 construction-supervision tender for UT-4/UT-5 (UA-2019-09-30-000369-a) also exist per search-engine indexing of prozorro.gov.ua, but both are JS-rendered SPA pages I could not resolve to their internal API IDs within this pass's effort budget -- their content is UNVERIFIED, flagged for a follow-up pass, not treated as a dead link. No source found confirms actual physical dismantling of any Du700 stretch, nor any status update after 2020 -- this corridor sits in Kharkiv/Donetsk oblast, active front-line territory since 2022, and I found no dated evidence either way on a wartime pause. A web-search snippet suggesting an 'October 2022 restoration' of a 'reserve Shebelinka-Slovyansk' pipeline was checked and is a MISREAD -- the only fetched primary confirms it refers to a DIFFERENT line, 'Shebelinka-Novopskov', whose valves Russian occupiers illegally shut on 11 May 2022 (lb.ua, 14.05.2022); that incident does not belong to this cluster. Currently the pair double-counts length in any roll-up: 70+54=124km of pipe recorded against a corridor whose own approved design documents put its total length at ~67-68.6km -- a ~54-56km overstatement risk as long as both rows are summed as separately 'operating'.

concerns.recommendation: Recommend to Update: reconcile P5989 (Taganrog-Melitopol, 272.73 km, operating since 2024) against P7817+P7818, which record the same Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk restoration at stale 'construction'/'proposed' statuses. The arithmetic and the reported build narrative line up too closely to be coincidence: P7817 (104.50 km) + P7818 (68.93 km) = 173.43 km for the restored Soviet trunk Taganrog->Mariupol->Berdyansk; P5989 minus that = 272.73 - 173.43 = 99.30 km, matching the independently reported 'more than 100 km' new Berdyansk-Melitopol extension (Kommersant, RIA Novosti). Kommersant's 2022-07-13 piece (kommersant.ru/doc/5459063, verified) describes the Russian Ministry of Energy's plan as explicitly TWO parts: (1) restore the existing but disused Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk trunk, (2) build a genuinely new >100 km Berdyansk-Melitopol section. That is exactly the geography P7817 (Taganrog-Mariupol, under reconstruction) + P7818 (Mariupol-Berdyansk, proposed extension) individually cover, and exactly the through-route P5989 now shows as completed and operating. No source anywhere in this search — including gem.wiki's own outbound citations, read only to harvest leads (2025 DNR Minstroy planning order confirming Taganrog-Mariupol 'underway' / Mariupol-Berdyansk 'proposed') — describes a SEPARATE, independently justified Taganrog-Melitopol asset distinct from the restored trunk plus its extension. Recommend Update fold P7817+P7818's status forward to match P5989 (i.e. treat them as superseded/merged into the now-operating P5989 corridor) or, if segment-level tracking is wanted, update P7817/P7818 statuses to 'operating' to match P5989 rather than carrying three simultaneous statuses (construction + proposed + operating) for one physical corridor. CONFIDENCE CAP: every source found is Russian state media or the DNR/Zaporizhzhia occupation administration (Kommersant, RIA Novosti, ura.news, which itself syndicates Kommersant) — one government announcement reprinted by aligned outlets is ONE origin per the corroboration rule; no Ukrainian government, ISW, or Western trade-press confirmation was found despite searching. Tier medium, not high, on the duplicate finding itself, though the arithmetic match is what makes it more than speculation.
concerns.researcher_notes: [cluster E — DUPLICATE_CONFIRMED: Cluster E (Taganrog family) — P5989 likely double-counts P7817+P7818 as a completed corridor; P1457's 516 km is unconfirmed; P1488 is unrelated] P5989's own two citations name only Taganrog and Melitopol (per the task brief) — neither names Mariupol nor Berdyansk, so the overlap is not provable from P5989's citations alone; it is established here by cross-referencing the independently reported build narrative and length arithmetic. Sources checked and verified live: kommersant.ru/doc/5459063 (2022-07-13, 'Российский газ дотянется до Запорожья' — states the >100 km Berdyansk-Melitopol figure and the two-part restore+extend plan, and that the old corridor 'was partially unused since the 2009 gas conflict' i.e. needs partial not full rebuild); ria.ru/20220719/gazoprovod-1803530880.html (2022-07-19 — Zaporizhzhia occupation head Yevgeny Balitsky announces the Berdyansk-Melitopol build, no length given); ria.ru/20221025/gaz-1826622360.html (2022-10-25 — gas reaches Berdyansk first, per occupation figure Vladimir Rogov, with Melitopol to follow); neftegaz.ru's follow-up (2022-10-31, gas begins flowing to Melitopol households) corroborates the completion date range but the page is JS-rendered and its live text could not be extracted for a substring check — cite with that caveat if used. All of the above ultimately trace to ONE Russian government decision (Deputy PM Khusnullin's July 2022 directive) reported through aligned state/occupation channels — this is single-origin, medium tier by the standing rule, not two independent origins. Owner/attribution flag: P5989 carries a blank Owner while 'operating'. No source names a specific legal operator for the restored/extended line — occupation-administration statements attribute oversight to Russia's Ministry of Energy (Minenergo) as the sponsoring federal body, not a named pipeline operator, and Gazprom is documented (neftegaz 2014 reporting) as the historical owner of the original 1950s Taganrog-Mariupol trunk only, before its 2009 closure — that attribution does not automatically carry to a post-2022 occupation-built asset. GEM should NOT default Owner to either the Gas TSO of Ukraine (which does not operate in occupied territory) or Gazprom (unsourced for this specific restored/extended asset) — leave Owner blank and document the ambiguity in ResearcherNotes rather than guessing.

That tension itself is the reconciliation question for Update: either the segment was substantially complete enough to pass gas by late 2022 while formal capital-works documentation continued into 2025, or the 2022 gas-delivery reporting and this row's 'construction' status cannot both be describing the same completed asset without a status update.
concerns.researcher_notes: [cluster E — DUPLICATE_CONFIRMED: Cluster E (Taganrog family) — P5989 likely double-counts P7817+P7818 as a completed corridor; P1457's 516 km is unconfirmed; P1488 is unrelated] 104.50 km merged length, 700 mm, Taganrog->Mariupol. This is plausible but unconfirmed; flagging as a spec question for Update rather than asserting it.

concerns.recommendation: No merge. Do not fold into P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod). Worth a one-line ResearcherNotes cross-reference since the two share a corridor for most of their route.
concerns.researcher_notes: Checked directly against the obvious candidate on the roster, P0768 Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod ('UPU'), because both are Soviet 1980s Yamalo-Nenets-to-Uzhhorod export trunks feeding the same Bratstvo/Brotherhood system. They are NOT the same pipe: different origin fields (P0774 = Yamburg field; P0768 = Urengoy field, ~250km apart), different diameters as recorded (1400mm vs 1420/1400mm), different capacities (26 vs 32 bcm/y), different construction years (1988 vs 1983), and Ukrainian Wikipedia is explicit that they are two separate physical pipes that happen to run in the same bundled corridor: 'Прогрес' 'сходиться на КС Ординська в Центральний газотранспортний коридор' with Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod (converges into the shared corridor at Ordynskaya CS), and after Yelets/that point 'Прогрес прямує разом з Уренгой — Помари — Ужгород' (Progress proceeds together with UPU). This is standard Soviet megaproject practice: multiple independently-built, independently-operated parallel strings sharing one right-of-way/bundle for hundreds of km, not a single pipeline recorded twice. Several low-quality Russian SEO aggregator sites (fb.ru, in.minsk.by) recycle the same '1160 km through Ukraine' figure for BOTH Progress and UPU, which is exactly what you'd expect if they share the Ukrainian-territory corridor length — consistent with 'parallel, not identical' rather than evidence of a double-count.

concerns.recommendation: Adjudicate P0777 against P1480 ('Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine Gas Pipeline') — do not merge unilaterally, flag for the cluster-level adjudication pass named in the sweep scope guidance.
concerns.researcher_notes: P0777 and P1480 are very likely the SAME real-world two-line system (КЗУ, above) recorded twice under near-identical names with mutually inconsistent breakdowns. Structural match: both rows are named 'Kyiv[-–]Western Border [of Ukraine] Pipeline', both start at Kyiv, and BOTH independently describe themselves as 'two strings' with the SAME diameter/vintage pattern — String I = 1020 mm / commissioned 1970, String II = 1220 mm / commissioned ~1972-73 — which is exactly the КЗУ-1 (1020mm, 1970)/КЗУ-2 (1220mm, 1973) pattern in Ukrainian Wikipedia's single-system article. That is too specific a coincidence (matching diameters AND matching String-I vintage) to be two unrelated pipelines. Yet the two GEM rows disagree hard on the numbers that would distinguish them: P0777 = String I 522 km + String II 590 km = 1112 km total, ending at Uzhhorod; P1480 = String I 183.6 km + String II 216.3 km = 399.9 km total, ending at Drozdovychi on the Ukraine/Poland border (a different corridor entirely — matches this roster's P0778 Komarno-Drozdovychi line, not the Uzhhorod/Bratstvo corridor Ukrainian Wikipedia associates with КЗУ-2). Possible explanations, none of which I resolved here per the sweep's rule not to adjudicate clusters solo: (a) GEM split one real system into two duplicate rows with fabricated/mis-derived length splits; (b) the two rows genuinely describe different physical branches (a Uzhhorod-bound export leg vs. a Drozdovychi/Poland-bound leg) that share a common Kyiv-area trunk section before diverging, in which case neither row alone is 'wrong' but the two need reconciled, non-overlapping length accounting; either way the current independent pair of totals (1112 + 399.9 = 1511.9 km) cannot both be full, non-overlapping physical distances without corroboration, since Ukrainian Wikipedia's own combined total for the whole КЗУ-1+КЗУ-2 system is only 873 km (367+506).

concerns.recommendation: flag for cluster-level adjudication, do not merge unilaterally — check P0783's Kremenchuk→Kryvyi Rih tail against P1460 (Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 700mm/272.2km) and P0783's Kremenchuk hub against P1485 (Kremenchuk-Anan'iv-Bohorodchany, 1020mm/532km)
concerns.researcher_notes: P0783 shares its 'Kremenchuk' hub node with two other roster rows, and the physical-corridor evidence is genuinely ambiguous, not something I should resolve alone. (1) P1460 'Dikanka-Kremenchuk–Krivyi Rih Gas Pipeline' (len=272.2km, dia=700mm) has the IDENTICAL Kremenchuk→Kryvyi Rih tail segment as P0783 (len=771km total, dia=1420mm) but a different origin (Dykanka UGS, not Yelets/Russia) and a much smaller diameter. Wikipedia's list of 'main pipelines of the southern transit corridor' names Yelets–Kremenchuk–Kryvyi Rih, Shebelinka–Dnipropetrovsk–Kryvyi Rih–Rozdilna–Izmail, Kremenchuk–Ananyiv–Bohorodchany, Ananyiv–Tiraspol–Izmail, and Rozdilna–Izmail — a 'Dykanka–Kremenchuk–Kryvyi Rih' line is NOT among them, which is odd if it is a fully separate named trunk. The differing diameter (700mm vs 1420mm) argues against a straight duplicate (more likely a parallel smaller-bore line on the same corridor, which is normal Soviet practice — c.f. the legitimate parallel Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II pair), but the identical tail routing means GEM may be double-counting the same physical right-of-way as two 'pipelines' when it is actually one trunk plus a parallel/feeder line, or P1460 may itself be a mislabeled/duplicate entity. (2) GulfPub's reconciliation (recon-gulfpub-20260812/match_diff.json) independently flags a segment 'Kremenchuk - Ananyev' (321.9km) as AMBIGUOUS between P0783 and P1485 ('candidates': P0783 composite 0.498, P1485 composite 0.465) — i.e. the automated matcher cannot cleanly separate which GEM row that continuation past Kremenchuk belongs to, and neither candidate clears the accept threshold on its own. This is exactly the kind of hub-node ambiguity the sweep brief flags for hand adjudication (cf. the Dikanka/Dolyna-hub clusters called out in the country guidance) — surfacing it here rather than silently assuming either P0783's or P1460's stated 771km/272km don't overlap.

concerns.recommendation: Flag for a cluster-level adjudication of the 'Izmail corridor' (P0784 vs P0786 Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail vs P0787 Rozdilna-Izmail) -- do not fold, delete, or re-spec P0784 unilaterally from this single-row pass.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's own wiki page for P0784 sources its three key numbers from three DIFFERENT, mostly off-topic citations, and none of the three actually describes a single distinct pipeline matching this row's name. Per the gem.wiki infobox/citation trail: Length=164km is sourced to ngpedia.ru (a page about the Shebelinka gas FIELD, not a route-length source); Diameter=1200mm is sourced to a prozorro.gov.ua procurement TENDER for the TSO corporate entity (a generic company-registration record, not a pipeline spec sheet); Capacity=24 bcm/y is sourced to Gainutdinova (2012), an academic article about Arctic/regional gas-market formation. I fetched the Gainutdinova article directly (cyberleninka.ru, verified live, independent of GEM) and it does NOT support a standalone 'Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Rozdilna-Izmail' pipeline at all: its export-capacity-at-western-border table has ONE combined row reading 'Ананьев - тирасполь - Измаил, Шебелинка - Измаил (три нитки) 24' (Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail, Shebelinka-Izmail (three threads) = 24 bcm/y to Romania/Bulgaria/Greece/Turkey/Macedonia) -- i.e. 24 bcm/y is an AGGREGATE figure spanning BOTH the Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail line (already tracked separately as P0786, itself 1200mm/23.7 bcm/y per its own GEM page citing KPMG 2017 -- essentially the whole 24 bcm/y already) AND a 'Shebelinka-Izmail (three threads)' system, not a capacity belonging to one pipeline named 'Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Rozdilna-Izmail'. Cross-checked against Ukrainian Wikipedia's 'Shebelinka-Izmail gas transport corridor' article (uk.wikipedia.org, verified live, independent secondary source citing Moldovatransgaz's own company history and a Moldovan government gasification-program document): the corridor's real named pipelines are (a) Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Odesa/-Odesa-2 (ШДО/ШДО-2), (b) Roздільна-Izmail, 820mm, commissioned Oct 1973 -- this is P0787, and (c) Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail (шдкрі, 'SHDKRI'), commissioned 1975 with TWO threads of 800mm each -- together SHDKRI + Rozdilna-Izmail could supply UP TO 15.8 bcm/y combined to the Balkans (per the cited Moldovan document), a figure that matches neither GEM's 24 bcm/y nor P0787's own 7.3 bcm/y. GEM's P0784 row name is a garbled fusion of the real SHDKRI route ('Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih') with the endpoint of the SEPARATE Rozdilna-Izmail line ('Rozdilna-Izmail') tacked on -- a name that does not correspond to any single pipeline in the sourced history. Its diameter (1200mm) and capacity (24 bcm/y) instead match P0786 (Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail, 1200mm/23.7 bcm/y) almost exactly, not SHDKRI's real 800mm/partial-15.8bcm/y or Rozdilna-Izmail's real 820mm. Most likely explanation: whoever built this GEM row read the Gainutdinova (2012) combined-corridor table row, split its two comma-separated route labels into two GEM entities, and (mis)assigned the SAME diameter/capacity pulled from Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail's own sourcing to the second (Shebelinka-Izmail) label, then invented a composite name blending SHDKRI with Rozdilna-Izmail. Two independent, non-GEM sources (Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article + the Gainutdinova 2012 academic article) corroborate this reconstruction; tier medium (both are secondary/tertiary, no single primary per-pipeline TSO document was found for SHDKRI specifically). This is NOT a claim that no real pipeline exists along the Shebelinka-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail route -- SHDKRI is real and built 1975 -- but P0784 AS RECORDED (this name + these specs) does not correspond to it, to Rozdilna-Izmail, or to Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail individually; it reads as a data-entry artifact straddling all three.

concerns.recommendation: cluster-level adjudication vs P0784 (do not merge/change unilaterally)
concerns.researcher_notes: Per the Izmail-corridor cluster note (P0784/P0786/P0787): Moldovatransgaz's own asset list gives its transiting section of the line it calls 'Шебелинка-Днепропетровск-Кривой Рог-Измаил (ШДКРИ)' — clearly the same name family as GEM's P0784 'Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Rozdilna-Izmail' — a diameter of 820 mm and a capacity of 7.3 bcm/y, i.e. IDENTICAL specs to P0787's Rozdilna-Izmail line (also 820 mm / 7.3 bcm/y) in the Moldovan segment (91.817 km, almost the same as P0787's Moldovan-segment 92.24 km). GEM's own P0784 record instead carries 1200 mm / 24 bcm/y and a total length of only 164 km — specs that belong to the big Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih trunk further upstream, not to the Rozdilna-Izmail tail leg that actually crosses into Moldova/Izmail. This is consistent with the two GEM rows sharing a common physical tail segment near Izmail (i.e., a possible partial double-count between P0787 and P0784), and separately confirms the standing note that P0784's 164 km total is implausible for a route spanning Shebelinka to Izmail. By contrast, P0786 'Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail' matches a DIFFERENT Moldovatransgaz line item ('Ananьев-Тирасполь-Измаил (АТИ)', 1220 mm / 20 bcm/y) and does not appear to overlap with P0787. Flagging for cluster adjudication, not resolving here — P0784 is outside this row's scope.

concerns.recommendation: no merge recommended -- checked against the Dikanka-family cluster (P1452/P1453/P1454/P1460) and found independent confirmation these are distinct parallel Soviet-era trunk lines converging on the Dikanka compressor-station hub, not a double-count; still worth including in any separate cluster-level adjudication pass per the standing instruction not to resolve clusters solo.
concerns.researcher_notes: Per the country scope guidance, checked P1454 against the 'Dikanka family' (P1452 Shebelinka-Poltava-Kiev 454.7 km/700mm, P1453 Efremovka-Dikanka-Kiev 477 km/1000mm, P1460 Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Krivyi Rih 272.2 km/700mm). The Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article independently confirms THREE distinct, separately-built parallel lines converging at Dikanka: Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv (700mm/478km/1961) = P1452, Yefremivka-Dikanka-Kyiv (1020mm/1970) = P1453, and Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kyiv (1220mm/550km/1973) = P1454 -- a classic Soviet multi-thread trunk buildout, the same pattern as the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II pair (P3484/P5938) noted in the country guidance. P1460 continues on beyond Dikanka toward Kremenchuk/Kryvyi Rih and is a downstream continuation, not an overlapping duplicate of P1454 which terminates at Kyiv. concerns.pipeline_name: Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine Gas Pipeline
concerns.recommendation: Flag for the cluster-level redundancy adjudication pass vs P0777 ('Kyiv–Western Border Pipeline') — do not merge or delete either row unilaterally.
concerns.researcher_notes: P1480 and P0777 are both named 'Kyiv–Western Border [of Ukraine] [Gas] Pipeline', both start at Kyiv, both are recorded as two strings with a 1020mm/~1970 first thread and a 1220mm/~1972-73 second thread — too specific a coincidence to be unrelated pipelines; they are almost certainly two GEM rows for pieces of the same real-world Kyiv–West Ukraine (КЗУ) trunk corridor. But the two rows' totals do not agree and, per P0777's own already-staged shard, cannot both be non-overlapping physical distances: P0777 = 522+590 = 1,112 km, ending at Uzhhorod; P1480 = 183.6+216.3 = 399.9 km (per the UTG chronology found here), with THIS row's gem.wiki page separately claiming an end point at Drozdovychi on the Ukraine/Poland border — a different corridor from Uzhhorod entirely. A third figure, Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated КЗУ article, gives 367+506 = 873 km for what it calls the identical named system. So there are THREE mutually inconsistent totals in circulation (1,112 / 873 / 399.9 km) for something called 'Kyiv–Western Border [of Ukraine]', and unlike P0777's numbers (which no independent source corroborates verbatim per its own shard), P1480's 399.9/1020,1220mm/1970,1972 figures DO have an exact primary-source match (UTG's own chronology, above) — which argues P1480 is not itself a fabrication, but that it and P0777 may be recording two different, or partially double-counted, definitions/segments of the same corridor (e.g., a narrower UTG-internal 'КЗУ' trunk designation vs. a broader 'Kyiv to the export hub at Uzhhorod' corridor that strings together multiple named trunks). I did not attempt to resolve which framing is correct — per the sweep's rule, that is a cluster-adjudication decision, not a single-row call. Also worth the adjudicator's attention: gem.wiki's claimed endpoint for THIS row (Drozdovychi, Lviv Oblast, on the Poland border) is not corroborated by any source I found and conflicts with the Uzhhorod/Bratstvo-system association that both Ukrainian Wikipedia and P0777's gem.wiki page give to the analogous second thread — Drozdovychi is also associated in current reporting with a MODERN (post-Soviet) Poland-interconnector investment project, unrelated to this 1970s Soviet-era trunk, so it may be an anachronistic/incorrect endpoint on the wiki page. This row's own sheet values do not currently include an EndLocation, so this is a caveat for the eventual location fill, not a live sheet error.

concerns.recommendation: Cluster-level adjudication needed vs P1485 (Kremenchuk-Anan'iv-Bohorodchany Gas Pipeline) -- do not merge without a human/geometry check.
concerns.researcher_notes: P1485 'Kremenchuk-Anan'iv-Bohorodchany Gas Pipeline' shares TWO of P1481's three named waypoints (Anan'iv, Bohorodchany) and the same diameter (1020 mm), differing only in capacity (8.7 vs P1481's 9.1 bcm/y) and length (532 km vs 333 km) and in prepending a third far-off waypoint, Kremenchuk (Poltava Oblast, central Ukraine -- several hundred km from Anan'iv in the opposite direction from Bohorodchany). Two ways this resolves: (a) genuinely different physical pipes that happen to share an Anan'iv-Bohorodchany leg name and diameter by coincidence of the regional grid, or (b) P1485 is a mislabeled/duplicated entry that folds in this line's Anan'iv-Bohorodchany leg under an inflated route description. The independent evidence I found for P1481 (Moldovatransgaz naming exactly 'Ananyev-Chernovtsy-Bogorodchany' as ONE specific, complete, cross-border trunk with capacity 9.1 bcm/y) argues P1481 is the more soundly documented of the two and stands on its own -- but I have not found equivalent independent documentation for P1485's Kremenchuk waypoint or its 532 km/8.7 bcm/y figures, so I can't rule out overlap. Flagging per the standing duplicate-hunting instruction; not resolving myself.

concerns.recommendation: cluster-level adjudication vs P1481 (Ananjiv-Bohorodchani Gas Pipeline, 333 km, 1020 mm, 9.1 bcm/y) — check whether P1481 double-counts the Ananiv-Bohorodchany half of this same 532.6 km trunk
concerns.researcher_notes: The Ukrtransgaz chronology (the operator's own line-by-line construction record for the whole Ukrainian network, spanning 1960s-1990s) names exactly ONE construction event for this corridor: 'магістральний газопровід Кременчук - Ананьїв - Богородчани довжиною 532,6 км, ∅1020 мм' (1986-87). It records no separate 'Ananiv-Bohorodchany' pipeline anywhere in the document. P1481 in the roster ('Ananjiv-Bohorodchani Gas Pipeline', Ananjiv->?, 333 km, dia 1020 mm, cap 9.1 bcm/y) shares P1485's exact diameter (1020 mm) and a very similar capacity (9.1 vs 8.7 bcm/y), and its endpoints (Ananiv -> Bohorodchany) are a strict subset of P1485's route (Kremenchuk -> Ananiv -> Bohorodchany). 532.6 - 333 = ~199.6 km, which would be a plausible Kremenchuk-Ananiv segment length. This has the classic signature of a segment-vs-network double count (the whole trunk recorded once as P1485 and its western half recorded again as P1481) rather than two genuinely distinct pipelines — but I have not found independent sourcing for P1481 itself in this pass, so I am flagging for adjudication rather than recommending a merge/fold outright, per the sweep brief's instruction not to resolve clusters solo.

concerns.recommendation: Flag for the redundancy-cluster adjudication pass, cross-reference P3382 ('Shebelinka–Slovyansk Gas Pipeline', len=54.0 dia=500). Do not merge unilaterally — my reading is these are two RELATED but likely physically distinct assets (old vs. new parallel pipe on the same corridor), not a simple double-count, but a human should confirm.
concerns.researcher_notes: P3381 and P3382 share the identical pipeline name in the sheet ('Shebelinka–Slovyansk Gas Pipeline') and are clearly the same named corridor, but the tsoua.com official project description resolves WHY the two rows carry different length/diameter rather than being a pure duplicate: TSOUA's own investment-project page describes replacing the original Du700 pipe with a NEW Du500 pipe laid PARALLEL to the existing route ('заміна труби Ду 700 ... на трубу Ду 500 ... шляхом прокладки паралельно існуючий трасі'), in sections UT-1 (km1.1-13.6), UT-2 (km13.6-26.1), UT-3 (km26.1-39.9) and UT-4 (km39.9-55.1) — and explicitly states the plan is to DISMANTLE the old Du700 pipe only AFTER the Du500 section is commissioned ('демонтування існуючого газопроводу ДУ 700 після прийняття в експлуатацію ділянки Ду 500'). Doing the arithmetic on the UT sections: (13.6-1.1)+(26.1-13.6)+(39.9-26.1)+(55.1-39.9) = 12.5+12.5+13.8+15.2 = 54.0 km — an EXACT match to P3382's LengthKnown=54.0 and DiameterUnits=500mm. This is too precise to be coincidence: P3382 is almost certainly GEM's entry for the new/parallel Du500 pipe covering exactly the UT-1–UT-4 corridor (km1.1–55.1), while P3381 (this row, 70km, Du700, built 1969) is the ORIGINAL full-corridor pipe. So the pair likely represents two related-but-distinct physical assets mid-transition (old full-length line + new partial-length parallel replacement under construction), analogous to the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II pattern rather than a straightforward double-count — BUT there is real double-count risk if/once the Du500 section is fully commissioned and the Du700 section over that same 54km stretch is formally dismantled per TSOUA's own stated plan: at that point P3381's full 70km would overlap the now-decommissioned middle of the corridor with P3382's 54km of live pipe, and P3381's Status/Length would need updating to reflect only the still-operating Du700 remainder (roughly km0-1.1 and km55.1-68.6/70, i.e. ~14-16km) rather than the full 70km. I could not verify whether the Du700 dismantling has actually happened as of 2026 (see spec/status caveat below) — leaving that determination, and the merge/no-merge call, to the cluster adjudication pass.

concerns.recommendation: Cluster-level adjudication vs P3381 (same name, same corridor). Do not delete either row — determine whether P3381 (Du700, 70.0 km, the pre-reconstruction pipe) should move to a replaced/retired status as the Du500 replacement (P3382) comes online segment by segment, or whether the two rows should be merged once the full corridor is Du500.
concerns.researcher_notes: P3382 and P3381 share the identical pipeline name 'Shebelinka–Slovyansk Gas Pipeline' and endpoints (Shebelynka, Kharkiv Oblast → Slovyansk, Donetsk Oblast). They are NOT two coexisting parallel lines — they are the SAME 67 km corridor at two points in its life. The wiki's own cited generic source (tsoua.com 'Potochni proekty' page, cite_note :0, backlinks=6 — could not verify live, tsoua.com returns HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and url_verifier) plus independent confirmation via WebSearch, Ukrainian Wikipedia (uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/Шебелинка_—_Слов'янськ_(газопровід)) and nashigroshi.org investigative journalism (2015-12-04) describe ONE reconstruction project: 'Reconstruction of the Shebelinka-Slovyansk gas pipeline (replacement of Du700 with Du500, km 1.1-68.0, length 67 km), Kramatorsk LVUMG, Donetsk Oblast', built in 1969 as a single Du700 line, being replaced in-place by a parallel Du500 pipe in five tendered sections: UT-1 (km1.1-13.6), UT-2 (13.6-26.1), UT-3 (26.1-39.9), UT-4 (39.9-55.1), UT-5 (55.1-68.6/68.0). Official government procurement records (ProZorro tender UA-2020-06-10-007174-b, UT-5 construction; UA-2019-09-30-000369-a, UT-4/UT-5 supervision) and a 2013 Ministry order (search.ligazakon.ua FIN87423) confirm this is one continuous corridor project, not two separate pipelines. GEM's P3381 (Du700, 70.0 km) is the pre-reconstruction/original pipe; P3382 (Du500, 54.00 km) is the Du500 replacement as far as it had been captured. Both are recorded 'operating' — if the replacement is complete along its whole length, the surviving Du700 stretches represented by P3381 may no longer physically exist (dug up and replaced), which would make P3381 a stale duplicate rather than a real coexisting asset; if the replacement is only partial, both may legitimately be 'operating' in different stretches of the same corridor, which GEM does not currently model (no start/end km markers distinguishing which stretch belongs to which row). Either way this is a genealogy/double-count risk for capacity and length roll-ups and needs a human cluster call, not a unilateral fix here.

concerns.recommendation: Flag for cluster-level adjudication against P1488 ('Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' rebuild, named in the sweep's occupied-territory guidance but outside this row's given roster) -- do not merge/edit unilaterally.
concerns.researcher_notes: The historical record shows this corridor is made of at least TWO distinct physical components, and P5989's own compound name ('Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk') plus its wiki slug (just 'Taganrog-Melitopol', no Berdyansk) suggest GEM may be folding them together or mis-splitting them against a sibling row. Gas reached Berdyansk 2022-10-25 and Melitopol 2022-10-31 per neftegaz, citing then-acting Zaporizhzhia governor Balitsky. The scope guidance for this sweep explicitly names 'the Russian-built Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk rebuild' as touching P1488 (not included in the 9-row roster I was given for direct comparison). If P1488 already records the restored old Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk segment, P5989 -- whose own name spans Taganrog...Berdyansk AND Melitopol -- risks double-counting that same restored trunk under a second, broader-named row. I have not resolved this (per the sweep's own rule not to adjudicate clusters solo); it needs a side-by-side compare of P5989 vs P1488 on endpoints/length/ConstructionYear.

concerns.recommendation: Add ResearcherNotes documenting the cross-border/interconnector function (VIP Bereg with Hungary's FGSZ, live since May 2020); resolve which upstream trunk actually feeds it before trusting either wiki narrative uncritically.
concerns.researcher_notes: The sheet (and gem.wiki, which frames it as the pipeline 'redistributing' gas 'within Ukraine') presents this purely as a domestic Ukrainian line. Independent sourcing shows it is actually the Ukraine side of an active international gas interconnector to Beregdaróc, Hungary — unified in 2020 into a joint GTSOU/FGSZ 'VIP Bereg' virtual point with bidirectional booked capacity (export UA->HU and import HU->UA). That is a materially different characterization than 'redistribution within Ukraine.' Recording StartLocation=Uzhgorod/EndLocation=Berehove (both Ukraine) is defensible AS FAR AS IT GOES if the row is meant to represent only the Ukrainian-side segment terminating at the border (matching the interconnection point's Ukrainian name 'IP Beregovo'), but the missing cross-border context is a real gap, not a nitpick — a reader of the sheet would not know this line has anything to do with Hungary. Separately, the two wiki-family sources disagree on provenance: gem.wiki says gas arrives via the Dolyna-Uzhhorod pipeline (17 bcm/y); Ukrainian Wikipedia's Berehove-Beregdaróc article says the currently active 1400mm connector was built in 1986 off the Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod trunk specifically (with the original 1975 800mm Dolyna-Uzhhorod-fed line kept as a separate, later-reactivated reverse-flow line). These aren't necessarily irreconcilable (both trunks converge in the Uzhhorod area) but the sheet's StartLocation='Uzhgorod' quietly papers over a real ambiguity about which trunk this branch taps.

concerns.recommendation: Update should re-examine PipelineType, EndLocation and FuelSource in light of the 1966 reversal: BOTH BBC and ru.wikipedia state that in 1966 this pipeline's flow was PHYSICALLY REVERSED and it stopped functioning as a Dashava-to-Moscow transmission corridor. Recommend either (a) updating PipelineType to reflect the current distribution role and EndLocation/EndCountryOrArea to reflect current Ukraine-only service (Kyiv/Zhytomyr/Ternopil oblasts per BBC), with a ResearcherNotes entry documenting the pre-/post-1966 history, or (b) at minimum adding a ResearcherNotes caveat if the row is deliberately kept as the historical as-built corridor. Do not silently leave PipelineType='transmission' and EndLocation=Moscow/Russia unexamined -- both are now stale claims about current function, not just possibly-imprecise history.
concerns.researcher_notes: MAJOR FINDING, not previously flagged in this row's history per the country note. Both BBC Ukrainian (2018) and ru.wikipedia's 'Дашава — Киев' article independently state: 'До 1966 года газопровод Дашава-Киев-Москва работал в восточном направлении. Но с открытием других мощных месторождений ситуация изменилась. Подземную магистраль подключили к первой нитке другого газопровода - Шебелинка-Полтава-Киев. Он стал работать как распределительный. После реконструкции шлейфов на компрессорных станциях газ пошел по трубам в обратном направлении - на запад.' (Until 1966 the pipeline ran eastward; after other gas fields opened it was connected to the Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv line and reconstructed to run WEST instead, becoming a DISTRIBUTION pipeline.) BBC states the pipeline currently (as of 2018) supplies natural gas to towns/villages of Kyiv, Zhytomyr and Ternopil oblasts -- i.e. its documented CURRENT function is a Ukraine-domestic western distribution asset, not a Dashava-to-Moscow transmission line. Independently, ru.wikipedia corroborates the 1966 reversal-to-distribution and additionally notes a 1959 interconnection with the 'Shebelinka-Belgorod-Kursk-Bryansk' pipeline (= roster P2387) feeding gas onward to Belarus/Lithuania/Latvia via the Bryansk-Moscow section. So since 1966 the row's two halves have functioned as separate systems: the Ukrainian half is a west-flowing regional distribution line (fed by the Shebelinka network, P1452/P2387), and the Bryansk-Moscow half in Russia is part of Gazprom/Mostransgaz's own Moscow-region gas ring (documented at length in that company's internal history publication, Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's 'Prometei' newsletter -- content reviewed for research leads via a Wayback capture but its PDF text failed automated url_verifier text-matching, likely because the archived PDF is a scanned/rasterized layout the verifier's simple text search doesn't parse cleanly, so it is NOT included in proposed_refs per the verify-before-cite rule; not asserting it's unusable, just unverifiable by the mechanical gate here). GEM's row bundles both eras/halves under one still-'operating', 'transmission', Moscow-terminating record with no note of the 1966 change. I am NOT calling this a duplicate or a phantom -- the physical pipe is real and (per BBC) still in service -- but the CURRENT classification/location/fuel-source triad looks stale relative to the sourced 1966 reconfiguration and deserves a human Update pass rather than a silent pass-through.

concerns.recommendation: the three named parties (Gas TSO of Ukraine / Gazprom PJSC / QazaqGaz + operating subsidiary Intergas Central Asia) are each independently correct for this genuinely tri-national line, but the Owner percentage split (Owner1=TSOU 100%, Owner2=Gazprom blank%, Owner3=QazaqGaz blank%) is internally inconsistent — 100% cannot be assigned to one owner while two more owners are also listed; recommend re-expressing this as segment-based ownership (each state entity owns ~100% of its own national section) in ResearcherNotes rather than as fractional co-ownership of one asset, or leaving all three percentages blank
concerns.researcher_notes: This is a genuinely cross-border line (Russia→Kazakhstan→Ukraine, per the existence findings above), so — unlike a wholly-domestic Ukrainian row — having Gazprom PJSC listed alongside Ukraine's TSOU is NOT itself the attribution red flag the country guidance warns about; it reflects the real multi-country asset. Checked piece by piece: (a) Ukraine's Gas TSO of Ukraine (TSOU) as post-2020 operator of the Ukrainian section is independently confirmed by en.wikipedia's well-footnoted 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine' article ('The system is owned by Government of Ukraine and operated by Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine'); (b) Intergas Central Asia JSC as operator of the Kazakhstan section is confirmed by its own official 'General Information' page, which lists the Soyuz MGP under its Uralsk Branch network; (c) QazaqGaz as Intergas Central Asia's 100%-owning parent is confirmed by QazaqGaz's own official corporate-structure page, which lists 'Intergas Central Asia JSC' under its 'Trunk transportation' subsidiaries; (d) Gazprom's role on the Russian section is supported more weakly — ru.wikipedia's navbox categorizes Soyuz among Gazprom's Russian main export trunks ('Магистральные газопроводы России' / 'Gazprom pipeline map'), which is standard but indirect. Given all three parties check out individually, I filled the Operator ref with these sources rather than marking UNRESOLVED, but the ownership PERCENTAGE structure (100% / blank / blank) is a real data-model inconsistency that predates this pass and that I could not resolve to a defensible split — I did not fabricate percentages for Owner2/Owner3, and I would not paste any percentage change without a source that states an actual ownership share (none of my sources state one; they state operator/subsidiary roles, not equity splits).

concerns.researcher_notes: [cluster H — DUPLICATE_REFUTED: Cluster H — Yelets-Kursk family (P0775/P0776): duplicate REFUTED; ownership-attribution defect confirmed as its own concern] DUPLICATE QUESTION: REFUTED. Two independent, non-GEM sources each name «Єлець—Курськ—Диканька» and «Єлець—Курськ—Київ» as separate 1220 mm trunk lines: (1) the Kursk Oblast district administration's official gas-corridor/security-zone listing (kurskr.rkursk.ru, archived 2022-05-19 at web.archive.org/web/20220519195206/http://kurskr.rkursk.ru/index.php?sub_menus_id=18020&id_mat=2996) states verbatim: '...Уренгой – Ужгород Ф1420мм, Елец – Курск – Диканька Ф1220мм, Елец – Курск – Киев Ф1220мм...' as two items in a corridor list, both 1220 mm — i.e. a Russian government body, independent of Gazprom, distinguishing them by name while giving them the SAME diameter, which rules out 'different diameter = different line, same diameter = the same line' as a shortcut; naming is what does the work here. (2) Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's own Kurskoe LPUMG page (moskva-tr.gazprom.ru/kurskoe-lpumg/, archived 2025-05-12) states in its historical-construction narrative: 'строятся магистральные газопроводы: «Елец — Курск — Киев», «Уренгой — Ужгород», «Елец — Курск — Диканька», «Елец — Кременчуг — Кривой Рог», магистральный газопровод «Прогресс»' — again both named as separate items in a list of distinct Soviet-era trunks built through the oblast. (3) uk.wikipedia's own dedicated article on «Єлець — Курськ — Диканька» (cites Kursk oblast admin, the Ukrtransgaz chronology, and two independent Lipetsk/Kursk regional gas-supply characterization documents) gives 1220 mm, 5.5 MPa, commissioned 1984 — matching GEM P0775's diameter and StartYear1 exactly. GEOMETRY (GEM's own drawn routes, corroborating from a fourth, independent-of-sourcing angle): P0775 and P0776 share only a 189.3 km Yelets-to-Kursk prefix, then physically diverge at Kursk (51.711, 36.157) — P0775 continues 239.0 km to Dykanka, P0776 continues 417.5 km to Kyiv, hundreds of km apart in different directions. That is the geometric signature of two lines sharing an origin/transit corridor, not one line recorded twice. CAPACITY (weaker, treat as single-origin, not independent corroboration): the live moskva-tr.gazprom.ru Kurskoe LPUMG page (fetched once successfully via curl with a browser UA on 2026-08-15; the site subsequently became intermittently unreachable to both direct fetch and archive.org's Save-Page-Now, which returned 523 origin-unreachable — this is a live-site availability problem, not a dead-link finding, and I could not get url_verifier.py to pass on the live URL for that reason) lists 'Елец-Курск-Диканька» диаметр трубы 1220 мм ... производительность 65 млн. м3/сут' and 'Елец-Курск-Киев» диаметр трубы 1220 мм ... производительность 45 млн. м3/сут'. 65 and 45 million m3/day annualize to 23.725 and 16.425 bcm/y — matching GEM's stated 23.73 and 16.43 bcm/y on P0775/P0776 almost to the decimal. That precision match is too exact to be coincidence, but it cuts the other way on independence: it suggests this same characteristics document (or a shared upstream) may be the actual origin of GEM's own capacity figures, so it should NOT be counted as a second independent source validating the capacity VALUES — only as further confirmation that the two lines are tracked as separate items with separate capacities. LENGTH: no source (this batch or the two Wikipedia/Gazprom/rkursk documents) gives an explicit km figure for either line, so the near-identical 298.00/297.00 km on the sheet remains UNSOURCED in both directions; the Ukrainian-territory-portion hypothesis from the brief is neither confirmed nor ruled out here (border-to-Dykanka is roughly 170 km and border-to-Kyiv roughly 380 km by my own rough estimate, neither close to ~297, but this was not independently sourced and should not be treated as a finding). MINOR SPEC NOTE: search snippets (not a dedicated article, so weaker/uncorroborated) give 1982 for the Kyiv line's commissioning vs GEM's StartYear1=1981 for P0776 — a one-year discrepancy worth a follow-up Update ref-sweep item, not a duplicate signal. ADJACENT CONTEXT (P0783, P1453): per route_geometry_findings.md's cluster-F test, P0783 (Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 1420 mm) does NOT geometrically concatenate from P0775+P1460 (0 of 3 P1460 vertices and only 1 of 3 P0775 vertices lie on P0783's trace), and the three rows carry three different diameters (1420/1220/700 mm) — the signature of distinct parallel pipes in a shared corridor, not a triple-count. That is cluster F's finding, not re-adjudicated here. P1453 (Yefremivka-Dykanka-Kyiv) is documented in kzu_evidence.md as part of the 1970 KZU-1 commissioning cohort, a third distinct line converging on the same Dykanka hub — consistent with Dykanka being a genuine multi-line junction, not evidence that any of these rows duplicate each other.

concerns.recommendation: Re-derive Length for this segment from a route-specific figure rather than the current straight-line city-to-city estimate; flag LengthEstimateKm=104.50 as likely overstated pending a sourced route length.

Granovsky describing 'the 33-kilometer main gas pipeline (MGP) "Taganrog-Mariupol", built in the 1950s and closed in 2009 after the Russia-Ukraine gas conflict,' and separately quotes a 2014 Gazprom liquidation tender for the object 'Магистральный газопровод Таганрог-Мариуполь 1 нитка 20,4-56,7 км' (i.e. km-marker range 20.4-56.7, a 36.3 km stretch). concerns.recommendation: no change to Capacity/Diameter, but note the sourcing profile in ResearcherNotes: capacity has a genuine design-vs-actual spread and diameter rests on one strong explicit source
concerns.researcher_notes: CAPACITY: GEM's 25.20 bcm/y is an EXACT match to Russia's official cdu.ru (Central Dispatch Directorate of the Fuel & Energy Complex) figure of '25,2 млрд куб. м в год' for the Soyuz line specifically — this is a strong, independent, authoritative confirmation and I would NOT change the value. This ~3% spread (25.2 vs 26/26.1) is the ordinary design-vs-actual-technical-capacity variance seen across Soviet-era trunks and is NOT treated as a material conflict requiring a value change — but it is real enough that I would not silently treat 25.2 as the only number that exists; flagging it rather than picking a winner. DIAMETER: GEM's 1420.00 mm is confirmed explicitly by ru.wikipedia's infobox ('Диаметр 1420 мм'), which is entirely consistent with 1420 mm being the standard USSR 'super-power' export-trunk diameter class used on the parallel Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod and Progress lines of the same era and capacity class. I could not independently corroborate the exact 1420 mm figure on a second source distinct from ru.wikipedia within this pass (neftegaz.ru and fb.ru describe the route/history/capacity but do not state diameter) — tier medium rather than high on diameter specifically, not because I found any conflicting figure, but because a second explicit citation is still worth chasing in a future pass.

This is a NEW false-positive family for url_verifier (digit-substring collision inside inline SVG markup on a blocked page) not yet covered in its docstring's known false-negative list. It means the sheet's own dominant cited source for this row (7 of its 3 citations' backlinks) cannot actually be verified by us right now, and any OTHER researcher who ran the same check on this URL would have been given a false green light. STOPYEAR: sheet has StopYear=2007. No independent source found states this specific year. What we DID confirm: Interfax (25 Jun 2019) reports both the Stavropol-Moscow and Saratov-Moscow mains as 'недействующими' (non-operational) with active physical liquidation of a 165km segment of Line II and a partial 22m liquidation of Line I (section 559.6-725km), contractor selection underway, completion targeted for December 2020 -- this corroborates 'retired' as the correct Status but gives no year for when it actually STOPPED carrying gas. 2007 is plausible (a pipe can sit idle for years before formal physical dismantlement begins) but is currently an unsourced number on the sheet; recommend leaving as-is (nothing found to contradict it) but sourcing it properly once a working alternative to energybase.ru is found, or by a researcher who can access energybase.ru from an unblocked network/IP.

concerns.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown (likely ~100-101 km, not 110 km) and Diameter (likely '1000' only, not '700, 1000'); leave SegmentCost UNRESOLVED rather than keep an unconfirmed 365,000,000 EUR figure
concerns.researcher_notes:
LENGTH: two independent primary planning sources agree closely with each other and disagree with the sheet. ENTSOG TYNDP 2020 Annex A gives Polish section = 'the exact length - 1,5km' (table shows 2 km rounded) plus Ukrainian section 'Drozdovychi - Bilche Volytsya' = 99 km -> total ~100.3-101 km. The Energy Community PLIMA page independently states 'The total length of the gas pipeline is 98.8 km' for the Ukrainian section specifically. These two sources -- one a technical ENTSOG database entry, one a narrative TSO-sourced project history -- triangulate on a total of roughly 100-101 km, not GEM's 110 km (a ~9-11% overstatement).

DIAMETER: the same two sources both give DN1000 (mm) for BOTH sections (Polish 'Hermanowice Node - PL/UA border pipeline... 1,000mm' and Ukrainian 'Drozdovychi - Bilche Volytsya... 1,000mm'). GEM's second diameter value, 700mm, traces to only one source in the whole citation set: the USEA/EE-NGP Three Seas catalogue (May 2021), which lists 'Poland: Length 99km, Diameter 1,000mm' and 'Ukraine: Length 72km, Diameter 700mm, Start point Bilche Volytsya, End point Hermanowice' (pdftotext -layout confirmed verbatim; url_verifier content-screen fails on this file too for the same documented large-PDF reason). But that catalogue's own 'Ukraine' row (72km/700mm) describes the identical Bilche-Volytsya-to-Hermanowice segment that BOTH other independent sources put at 98.8-99km/1000mm -- i.e. the catalogue's figures for this one project look like a transcription/country-mislabelling error (it even puts a 99km value under 'Poland' that matches the true UKRAINIAN section length from the other two sources), not a genuine second pipe diameter. I could not find any source describing an actual DN700 segment of this specific interconnector. Recommend treating '700' as spurious and the diameter as DN1000 throughout, pending a fourth source if one turns up.

SEGMENTCOST: GEM records 365,000,000 EUR with no ref. The sheet's own cited 24tv.ua source (Ukrtransgaz CEO statement, Jan 2020) puts the Ukrainian-territory construction cost at approximately $245 million (and separately quotes the CEO asking 'sense in building... for $200 million'), which is roughly 220-230M EUR at contemporary exchange rates -- a ~35-40% gap from the sheet's 365M EUR, for a cost that in any case only covers the Ukrainian side. Both ENTSOG TYNDP and the Three Seas catalogue record CAPEX as 'n/a' for this project. No source corroborates 365,000,000 EUR; recommend leaving SegmentCost's ref UNRESOLVED rather than pairing a fabricated/unverified citation with it.

By contrast, StartYear1=2022 (TYNDP: 'Commissioning 2022' both sections; Ukrinform 2017 headline: Poland 'expects... to be put into operation by at most October 2022'), FIDStatus=Pre-FID (TYNDP labels the project 'Non-FID' throughout; Energy Community page: 'FID about this project was not taken'), and Capacity=8.00 bcm/y (24tv.ua's CEO quote frames the project as '5-8 billion cubic meters yearly'; the Energy Community page's Ukraine-side border capacity of 215 GWh/d is consistent with the upper end of that range) are all corroborated and staged as fills below -- this concern is scoped to Length/Diameter/SegmentCost only.

concerns.recommendation: correct Diameter 27.60 in -> 27.56 in (precise conversion of the sourced 700 mm) and add a ref; do not use the Romanian-side cost figures for SegmentCost
concerns.researcher_notes: DIAMETER is the metric-round-trip-with-false-precision defect the scope note warned about (same family as P1465/P3063). CAPACITY (7.70 MMSCMD): ENTSOG lists the capacity increment at the Siret(RO)/Khotyn(UA) point as 58.10 GWh/d (RO->UA) and 87.10 GWh/d (UA->RO). Converting GWh/d to MMSCMD with the standard ~11 kWh/Sm3 gas heating-value convention gives roughly 5.3 and 7.9 MMSCMD respectively -- the sheet's 7.70 MMSCMD sits within ~3% of the UA->RO (export) figure, which is a reasonable match given the conversion-factor approximation; treated as confirmed, single-source. SEGMENTCOST (40,000,000 EUR) could NOT be corroborated. All cost figures found in Transgaz's own planning documents (125M EUR in the 2018-2027 plan, 150M EUR in 2021-2030, 450M EUR in the new 2026-2035 plan) price the much longer 130-146 km ROMANIAN section (Gheraesti-Siret), a different segment/different GEM entity -- applying any of those numbers to this 30 km Ukrainian spur would be wrong. ENTSOG's financial-assistance fields for TRA-N-502 show no grant/cost figures either (both 'Grants for studies/works amount: Mln EUR 0.0', i.e. not applicable, not a cost estimate). No independent figure for a 40M EUR Ukrainian-side cost was found anywhere in the source ladder (tsoua.com, the TSO of Ukraine's own network-development-plan PDF, is Cloudflare-gated -- 403 to every UA tried, including the Wayback copy which also failed to fetch in time); leave SegmentCost as UNRESOLVED rather than force a source onto an unverified number.

concerns.recommendation: Do NOT delete. (4) Diameter 1200mm has the most solid direct sourcing of the four fields — a live, reachable ProZorro capital-repair tender for this exact pipeline gives DN1200 at km 108.5-111 near its Shebelinka-area origin — but the same trunk tapers to ~800-820mm by the time it reaches the Balkan-bound outlet near Izmail (per Moldovatransgaz's 820mm reading of the transiting tail and the Ukrainian wiki's 'two threads of 800mm' at 1975 commissioning); note the tapering diameter in ResearcherNotes rather than treating either figure as simply wrong.
concerns.researcher_notes: [cluster B — PARTIAL_OVERLAP: Izmail corridor (P0784/P0786/P0787) — three distinct pipelines; P0784 is a Frankenstein row needing rewrite, not deletion] GEM's own outbound citations for this exact wiki page (read under standing rule 4 — for outbound cites only, never cited here as a source) trace each of P0784's four data fields to a DIFFERENT, unrelated origin — the signature of a Frankenstein row, not a duplicate: Capacity 24 -> cyberleninka.ru (Gainutdinova); Length 164km -> ngpedia.ru; Diameter 1200mm -> a ProZorro tender; Name -> an apparent fusion of ШДКРІ's real corridor with 'Rozdilna', a waypoint that belongs to a different line (P0787). concerns.recommendation: flag Capacity=22 bcm/y and Status=operating for Update review — verify current cross-border throughput, don't just re-confirm nameplate diameter
concerns.researcher_notes: CAPACITY: GEM's 22.00 bcm/y matches isans.org's stated figure exactly (already the sheet's own working ref: 'gazoprovod «Torzhok — Dolina» diametrom 1420 mm (okolo 22 mlrd kub.m. v god)' — tier=medium as a single source, since I could not independently corroborate the 22 bcm figure a second time (belarus-tr.gazprom.ru and btg.by, both cited by gem.wiki for this row, are geo-blocked/unreachable from here — ConnectTimeout, consistent with the sheet's own existing_ref_checks). BUT this 22 bcm/y reads as a NAMEPLATE/diameter-implied design figure, not achieved throughput: Ukrainian Wikipedia's well-footnoted article states the pipe's linear section (incl. 529 km through Ukraine) was completed by 1995-1996 WITHOUT compressor stations, so the as-built system capacity was only ~6 bcm/y — not the ~22 bcm/y the 1420mm diameter would imply with full compression — and Ukraine repeatedly proposed finishing the 4 compressor stations needed on its territory in the early 2000s, but Russia chose pipeline routes bypassing Ukraine instead, so it was never completed. As of 2007 (the most recent figure the source gives) actual throughput was only 1.5-2.7 bcm/y — roughly one-tenth of the recorded Capacity value. STATUS: Status=operating needs a fresh look, not a rubber stamp. This line's documented purpose is carrying Russian-origin gas from Torzhok across Belarus INTO Ukraine at Dolyna. Ukraine has made zero direct purchases of Russian gas since 25 Nov 2015 (well-established, near-universally reported Ukrainian gas-sector fact, confirmed independently of this pipeline) — which, given the line's stated function, implies the cross-border (Belarus→Ukraine) flow direction has likely been dormant for roughly a decade, on top of the pre-existing compressor-station shortfall. I found no DATED source describing this specific line's status after 2007 (the ngsrb.com repair project, 2016-17, is on the RUSSIAN section near Torzhok itself and doesn't tell us about the cross-border flow), so per the country brief I'm not asserting a status change on general-transit grounds alone — but this is exactly the kind of row that deserves a targeted follow-up: does the pipe still carry any gas across into Ukraine today (e.g. reverse/local use, feeding the Mozyr UGS in Belarus without crossing the border), or has the Ukrainian portion effectively been idle since 2015-2022 despite still being 'physically operating' pipe.

concerns.recommendation: Do not treat 13.00 bcm/y as settled. Have a researcher reconcile against GTSOU/FGSZ's currently published entry-exit capacities (ENTSOG Transparency Platform is the cleanest live source) rather than banking the wiki figure.

None of these three numbers agree with each other or with the sheet's 13.00, and they aren't obviously reconcilable as the same measurement (nameplate vs. table vs. current firm+interruptible booking capacity, one-way vs. bidirectional). I did not find two sources that independently AGREE on 13.00, so I am not proposing a ref for the existing value, and I am not substituting a different number myself (no single figure here is clearly 'the' answer to the same question the sheet is asking). concerns.recommendation: Re-verify current Status before treating 'operating' as settled; document the occupation/valve-closure history in ResearcherNotes regardless of what Status ends up as.
concerns.researcher_notes: This is dated, line-specific evidence, not a generic 'transit stopped' inference (per the country guidance's rule against that). lb.ua (2022-05-11, already cited on the sheet's own gem.wiki page, re-verified live) reports Russian occupying forces closed valves on the 'Shebelinka-Novopskov' pipeline: the head of the Gas TSO of Ukraine stated the closure 'deprived Ukraine of the ability to transport gas to consumers of Luhansk and Donetsk regions,' and the article frames the valve closure as occurring on occupied territory (Novopskov / Starobilsk Raion, Luhansk Oblast, fell under Russian control in the 2022 invasion). I did NOT find any more recent, dated reporting on this specific line's status after May 2022 within this pass, so I cannot confirm whether the line has resumed carrying gas, sits idle, or is under Russian operation. Given the pipeline's Novopskov end lies in territory outside Ukrainian government control, 'operating' -- read as 'the Ukrainian state operator is actively running this asset' -- is at minimum unconfirmed for the post-2022 period, even though the physical pipe almost certainly still exists. I am NOT recommending a Status change without more current, line-specific evidence (per the standing instruction not to retire a line on transit-cessation grounds alone) -- flagging for a follow-on check with more recent sourcing, and recommending the occupation/valve-closure history go into ResearcherNotes either way.

concerns.recommendation: change StartYear1 from 1985 to 1986 (initial commissioning) or 1987 (full 532.6 km / 1020 mm completion, matching GEM's recorded spec) — verify which convention the tracker wants
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM records StartYear1=1985. The Ukrtransgaz chronology instead places this pipeline's commissioning at 1986 ('1986 р. Введено в експлуатацію магістральні газопроводи ... Кременчук - Ананьїв – Богородчани') with the full-spec entry (532.6 km, 1020 mm — the numbers matching GEM's current record) dated 1987. 1985 in the same document is the completion year for a DIFFERENT, nearby item — the Bohorodchany compressor station ('1985 р. Закінчено будівництво і введено в експлуатацію КС Богородчани') — which looks like the likely source of the sheet's 1985 date being confused with a compressor-station completion rather than the linear pipeline's own commissioning.
