concerns.recommendation: Do not treat StartYear1=1999 as settled. The one dated source found on the construction period says the line was built 1990–1998 (i.e. plausibly completed 1998, a year earlier), and it also gives a distinct 1978 founding date for the Makeevka linear production directorate that historically operated it — a fact that must not be conflated with the pipeline's own build year. Recommend Update search Soviet-era gas-industry engineering literature (per the country source ladder §6) for a primary construction record before changing StartYear1 either way; flagging as an open disagreement rather than proposing a replacement value off a single source.
concerns.researcher_notes: neftegaz.ru (2015) states: 'МГП Ду 1000 Краматорск - Донецк - Мариуполь строился в период 1990 - 1998 гг. и до войны относился к Макеевскому линейному производственному управлению магистральных газопроводов (ЛПУМГ), созданному в 1978 г.' (the pipeline was under construction 1990-1998, and before the war belonged to the Makeevka LPUMG, created in 1978). This is one source only for the pipeline's own build period — could not find a second independent source giving a construction/commissioning date, so this is not yet a resolved corroborated finding, just a live disagreement with the sheet's 1999 that Update should chase rather than silently accept. Note the 1978 date in the same sentence is for the operating directorate's founding, not the pipe itself — GEM's StartYear1 should never be backfilled from that number.

concerns.recommendation: No change to Capacity (keep 10.00 bcm/y). Do not treat the 8-9 bcm/y figure as a live conflict -- it is a superseded preliminary estimate from the same origin, not an independent competing claim.
concerns.researcher_notes: Kyiv Post/Interfax-Ukraine (28 Apr 2014, five months BEFORE commissioning) quoted Eustream's own network chief giving a preliminary technical estimate: the pipeline would be used 'at a maximum capacity of 8-9 billion cubic meters of gas per year.' At the actual commercial launch (2 Sep 2014), Eustream's own press release gives the confirmed, more precise figure: 'Vojany-Uzhorod pipeline will transport to Ukraine 10 bcm of natural gas per year (27 mcm/day)... The full capacity of 10 bcm/year...', with a minimum guaranteed volume of 6.4 bcm/y (17.6 mcm/day) from 1 Oct 2014 and firm capacity from 1 Mar 2015. GEM's value (10.00 bcm/y) matches the final authoritative figure exactly. Both numbers trace to the same origin (Eustream), so per the corroboration rule this is NOT two independent sources agreeing on 10 -- it is one source (Eustream) whose own estimate evolved between April and September 2014. Flagged for transparency, not as an unresolved conflict.

concerns.recommendation: Leave Diameter [ref] UNRESOLVED rather than cite a source that fails the verifier. If a future pass has ICIS access some other way, or finds an Eustream technical/network-map source with a diameter figure, add it then.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's own wiki page cites ICIS (the same 'Budince interconnector' article discussed above) as its sole source for Diameter=700mm ('single 700mm pipeline, which was quickly built by Eustream in 2013'). That source is real and was readable via an alternate fetch path for lead-following, but it fails scripts/url_verifier.py every time tried (200 status but a 210-850 byte stub body -- a bot-block/paywall, not a 404) and per the hard requirement 'every URL passes url_verifier.py before going in the xlsx,' it cannot be cited. No alternative source with an explicit diameter figure was found (Kyiv Post and both Eustream press releases give capacity but not diameter). Weak circumstantial corroboration only: ENTSOG/GIE System Capacity Map 2026 (sources/entsog/, already in this repo) classifies an operational pipeline strand in the Vojany/Uzhhorod border corridor (~22.22 E, 48.60 N) as its 'DN600-900 (24 to 36 in)' size class, which 700mm (~27.6 in) falls within -- consistent with, but not independent proof of, the exact 700mm figure. Net effect: the GEM value is plausible and not contradicted, but currently has NO independently verifiable public citation. Staged as UNRESOLVED, not as a value change.

concerns.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 1960 to 1959 (or 1958 if the Belgorod-only milestone is preferred)
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM records StartYear1=1960, but THREE independent non-GEM sources put this pipeline's own commissioning a year earlier and none supports 1960: Kurskaya Encyclopedia (mke.su) — 'В июле 1959 г. состоялось окончание работ по прокладке' (pipe-laying completed July 1959) and 'В ноябре-декабре 1959 г. началась эксплуатация' (industrial operation began Nov-Dec 1959); Spravochnick.ru — construction 'Completed in 1959; в этом же году началось его промышленное использование' (industrial use began that same year, 1959); Ukrainian Wikipedia — gas reached Belgorod already in 1958 ('сюди ресурс надійшов вже у 1958-му'), with the line completed to Bryansk in the late 1950s. The ONLY appearance of '1960' in any source is for a DIFFERENT, unrelated event: uk.wikipedia states the southern section of the SEPARATE Dashava-Kyiv-Bryansk-Moscow pipeline was reversed so Shebelinka gas could reach Kyiv from 1960 ('шебелинський газ зміг надходити до Києва з 1960-го, ще до завершення прямого газопроводу Шебелинка – Київ') — that is about Kyiv supply via a different trunk, not this pipeline's own construction date. GEM's 1960 looks like a conflation of the two facts. This is a material date discrepancy, not a rounding difference.

concerns.recommendation: record as a multi-value diameter (700, 800, 1020 mm) per the tracker's multi-value convention, or add a ResearcherNotes caveat — do not overwrite the sheet with a single figure
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's single Diameter=1020mm is technically one of the real diameters on this system but materially UNDERSTATES it: per Ukrainian Wikipedia, the system was built as two parallel lines — 'Первісно тут проклали нитку діаметром 700 мм (трубопровід ШБКБ I), яку невдовзі доповнили другою ниткою в діаметрі 800 мм (ШБКБ ІІ). В подальшому ШБКБ ІІ підсилили лупінгом діаметром 1020 мм' (originally a 700mm line [ShBKB I], soon supplemented by an 800mm second line [ShBKB II], later reinforced by a 1020mm looping) — i.e. three different diameters across the corridor's history, not one pipe. A FOURTH, newer diameter is also documented: Interfax (2022, Rostekhnadzor-approved reconstruction) and Spravochnick.ru both describe a new ~44km bypass/loop built 2020-2022 at ~1200mm (uk.wikipedia gives 1220mm for the same new loop: 'лупінгом довжиною 44 км та діаметром 1220 мм'). So the corridor now carries at least four historical diameters (700/800/1020/~1200mm) across parallel threads, and a bare '1020' materially undersells the asset even though it isn't 'wrong' per se.

concerns.recommendation: Verify whether Capacity=7062.93 MMcf/d (=200 mcm/d, converted from a round metric figure) and Diameter=1400mm describe ONE physical line or the AGGREGATE of the multi-line Uzhhorod/Veľké Kapušany crossing. Also cross-check against the 'Uzhhorod exit' duplicate cluster (P0780 / P1489 -- named in the orchestrator's scope guidance, outside this pass's 9-pipeline roster) and against the separately-named 'Vojany-Uzhhorod' reverse-flow interconnector (~10 bcm/y, built/upgraded 2014) at the cluster-adjudication pass. Do not apply a Capacity/Diameter/Length ref off this pass's evidence.
concerns.researcher_notes: Independent sources describe the Uzhhorod<->Veľké Kapušany border crossing as a MULTI-LINE bundle, not a single 1400mm/14.5km pipe: EP Power Europe states the transmission system at Veľké Kapušany consists of 'four to five parallel pipelines mostly 48/56 inches in diameter' (=~1219mm/1422mm) operating at 7.35 MPa; the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies paper (citing ENTSOG and IEA data) gives the COMBINED capacity of the 'Velké Kapušany (Ukraine-Slovakia)' connection as 189.0 mmcm/d (ENTSOG) / 197.5 mmcm/d (IEA) = 69.0/72.1 bcm/y -- close to, but not identical to, GEM's 200 mcm/d (=73.03 bcm/y, itself a suspicious round-number metric-to-imperial conversion per the country-wide flag on this exact row). A separate press trail (Eustream 2014 inauguration release; The Moscow Times, 2 Sep 2014, 'Slovak Gas Pipeline Offers New Reverse Supply Route for Ukraine') names a DISTINCT, smaller asset: the 'Vojany-Uzhhorod interconnector', built/upgraded specifically for east-bound reverse flow, running 'from the Vojany power station near the Ukrainian border to the western Ukrainian town of Uzhgorod' with a stated capacity of 'up to 10 billion cubic meters... a year' (~27.4 mcm/d) -- an order of magnitude smaller than GEM's 200 mcm/d, and with a different Slovak-side endpoint name (Vojany, not Velke Kapusany, though the 2014 inauguration ceremony itself was held at the CS in Veľké Kapušany, so the two places are closely linked/adjacent within the same hub). I cannot resolve from open sources whether GEM's P3063 (1400mm / 14.5km / 200 mcm/d) is meant to represent: (a) the aggregate of the whole historic multi-line crossing (in which case the single 1400mm diameter and 14.5km length materially understate the true 4-5-line asset), (b) one representative line within that bundle (plausible: 1400mm rounds close to the stated 56in/1422mm class), or (c) is being conflated with the separate, much-lower-capacity 2014 Vojany-Uzhhorod reverse-flow line. The 14.5km length is at least geographically plausible (Uzhhorod to Veľké Kapušany is ~15-20km airline distance), so LENGTH is not flagged as wrong, only unverified at that precision. This is exactly the kind of ambiguity the orchestrator's scope guidance calls out for the 'Uzhhorod exit' family (P0780 / P1489 / P3063) -- flagging for the redundancy/cluster-adjudication pass rather than resolving unilaterally.

concerns.recommendation: No value change proposed. Flag for future monitoring: TSOUA's own 2021 plan calls for eventual full dismantling of the Du700 pipe once its Du500 parallel replacement is commissioned corridor-wide; if that has since occurred, both LengthKnown (currently 70.00km, full corridor) and Diameter (700mm) would need revisiting to reflect only the surviving Du700 remainder. No dated evidence found that the dismantling has actually happened, so I am not proposing a change now.
concerns.researcher_notes: Length: sources cluster tightly around 67-68.6km for the corridor rather than exactly matching the sheet's 70.00km — Ukrainian Wikipedia and the ProZorro tender title both give '67 km' (km1.1 to km68.0), and TSOUA's own project text extends the reconstruction scope to km68.6 (i.e. ~67.5km from km1.1, or ~68.6km including the initial approach). A ~2-3km / ~3-4% gap from the sheet's 70.00km is not large enough on its own to call material (well under the >10% material-conflict threshold used elsewhere in this project), and is plausibly just a difference in where the corridor's km-0 reference point sits (technical km-markers along the pipe vs. straight-line/as-built distance) — so I am treating 70.00km as reasonably corroborated rather than wrong, with this noted as a minor caveat. Diameter: 700mm is solidly confirmed AS-BUILT (1969) by all three existence sources, but is NOT necessarily the CURRENT diameter along the whole corridor — TSOUA's 2021 document already describes km1.1-26.1 (UT-1/UT-2) as completed replacement to Du500, with UT-3/UT-4 (km26.1-55.1) 'ongoing', and further reconstruction of km55.1-68.6 to Du500 as still needed at that time, culminating in planned dismantling of the Du700 pipe. That means by the time of my research (2026), the physical pipe recorded as 700mm here may already be partially or wholly superseded/removed over some or all of its length — but I found no 2023-2025 source confirming project completion or dismantling one way or the other (Ukrainian search turned up no post-2021 status update specific to this project; the front-line proximity of Sloviansk since 2022 makes verification harder and also raises independent doubt about whether reconstruction work continued). Recommend leaving Diameter=700mm as-is (still the best-supported, most recently confirmed figure) but flagging this row for a repeat check once the war situation allows better visibility.

concerns.recommendation: Do not fill Length as confirmed. Verify whether GEM's 54.00 km is meant to represent km 1.1–55.1 of the corridor (UT-1 through UT-4, which sums to exactly 54.0 km) while the UT-5 stretch (km 55.1–68.6, ~13.5 km, tendered for construction in 2020 — the same year as GEM's ConstructionYear field) is missing from this row. If UT-5 has since completed, Length should move toward the full ~67 km corridor figure (or split logic should be documented) rather than staying at 54.00 with no ref.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM records LengthKnown=54.00 km with no citation. Independent sourcing (Ukrainian Wikipedia, nashigroshi.org, and ProZorro/Ligazakon procurement records surfaced via WebSearch — the ProZorro tender pages themselves are JS-rendered SPAs that return only ~800 bytes to a plain fetch and could not be independently re-verified live, so they are NOT cited as refs, only used as directional leads) consistently describe the reconstruction as covering the FULL corridor, km 1.1 to km 68.0, length 67 km — not 54 km. The five tendered sub-sections (UT-1 through UT-5) sum to ~66.9 km ≈ 67 km, matching the official project title. However, UT-1+UT-2+UT-3+UT-4 alone (km 1.1 to km 55.1) sums to exactly 54.0 km, and UT-5 (km 55.1–68.6) was tendered for construction on 2020-06-10 — the same year GEM's ConstructionYear field records for this row. This is a strong (though not certain) signal that GEM's 54.00 km captures only the first four of five reconstruction sections, undercounting the full corridor by roughly 13 km (~19%). Diameter (500 mm) is well corroborated for the replacement pipe by both independent sources and is fillable; Length is not — flagging as a material spec concern rather than confirming it.

concerns.recommendation: Verify LengthKnown against a fetchable authoritative source; current sheet value (292.00 km) is suspect and may need correcting to ~146 km. Do not apply a fix without an independently verifiable citation.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's sheet records LengthKnown=292.00 km for this row (P3484, segment I) and the SAME 292.00 km for P5938 (segment II) — i.e. both parallel threads carry an identical length figure that happens to equal 2x146. GEM's OWN gem.wiki mirror of this exact pipeline (fetched directly, raw HTML, last regenerated 2024-09-16 per the sheet's own 'updated' date, so contemporaneous with the current row) instead shows 'Length: 146 km each' for BOTH segment I and segment II — exactly half the sheet's current value. That wiki figure cites footnote [11] = eegas.com/belarus1.htm, but I fetched eegas.com/belarus1.htm directly (raw HTML) and it contains NO length/km figures at all for this pipeline — only diameter and thread-count ('2 x 1220 mm'). So the wiki's 146 km citation is itself misattributed/unsupported, meaning I cannot confirm 146 km through that chain either. I then tried to reach the likely original source: multiple independent web-search syntheses point to a UNECE/ENVSEC 'Environmental safety of main pipelines in Belarus' assessment (unece.org/sites/default/files/2025-08/_ENG__ENVSEC_EE_pipelines_project_Assessment.pdf) which reportedly states this pipeline is '146 km, 2 strings, 1220mm, built in 1976/1981' — years that match GEM's own StartYear1=1976 exactly, which is a meaningful corroborating detail. However I could NOT independently verify this: the PDF returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge) to both a direct fetch and WebFetch; no Wayback Machine capture exists yet, and a fresh Save Page Now attempt returned 520 (IA cannot reach the origin either) — so per standing rule 2/3 I cannot cite it and have not staged a fill. Net assessment: the sheet's 292 km is unconfirmed and contradicted by GEM's own wiki mirror of the same row (146 km), and the 2x relationship (146x2=292) is exactly the shape of a 'combined two-thread total pasted into a single thread's field' data-entry error. Flagging as a spec concern for a human pass with access to the UNECE PDF (or another route past its Cloudflare challenge) rather than applying an unverified number myself.

concerns.recommendation: Do not change GEM's Capacity value (1.30 bcm/y already matches the operator's current published figure) but flag the historical figure for awareness in ResearcherNotes: verify whether the line was ever formally uprated from its original 1966 design capacity, or whether one of the two company sources is simply carrying a stale/incorrect number.
concerns.researcher_notes: SPEC discrepancy on Capacity, >2x, between two sources from the same Moldovan state-gas corporate group. Moldovatransgaz's current network-overview page (mtg.md/ru/news/54) states the Odesa-Chisinau line's capacity as 1.3 billion m3/year — matching GEM exactly. But Moldovagaz's (the parent JSC) own GRS-1 Chisinau history article (moldovagaz.md) states the pipeline's ORIGINAL 1966 design throughput ('проектная производительность') as 570.0 million normal m3/year (=0.57 bcm/y) — less than half GEM's figure. Both texts otherwise agree exactly on length (44 km) and diameter (530 mm/Ду530), so this isn't a different pipeline being conflated. Two readings are possible: (a) the line was uprated at some point post-1966 from 570 to 1,300 million m3/y (no documentation of such a project found in this pass), or (b) one of the two company sources has carried forward an error. Because GEM's own value matches the CURRENT operator page exactly, I am not proposing a value change — but this is a genuine, material, unresolved disagreement between two sources in the same corporate family, not a clean confirmation, so it is flagged per the material-disagreement rule rather than silently passed.

concerns.recommendation: Re-derive per-thread Capacity and LengthKnown for both P3484 and P5938 -- do not leave the combined two-thread total stamped identically on each thread's own row. Route to Update.
concerns.researcher_notes: Both Capacity (29.00 bcm/y) and LengthKnown (292.00 km) are recorded IDENTICALLY on P5938 (this row, Thread II) and on P3484 (Thread I) -- i.e. the exact same numbers appear twice, once per thread. That is only correct if 29 bcm/y and 292 km are each thread's OWN individual spec. The evidence says they are not: (1) GEM's own gem.wiki infobox for this pipeline (read for leads only, never cited) labels Capacity explicitly as '29 bcm/y (total for the pipeline)' for BOTH Thread I and Thread II, i.e. the wiki editors themselves flagged 29 as the COMBINED two-thread figure, not a per-thread one -- yet the sheet stamps that combined total onto each thread's row, which would double-count system capacity to 58 bcm/y. (2) The independent iSANS 2023 report states the combined Ivatsevichi-Dolina two-thread system moves 'about 30 billion m3 per year' (около 30 млрд куб. м. в год), matching the sheet's 29 bcm/y as a SYSTEM total, not a per-thread figure -- corroborating (1) from a source independent of GEM. Neither btg.by nor eegas.com gives a bcm/y figure for this specific line, so I could not find a source that actually supports 29 bcm/y as each thread's own capacity; the only sourced capacity figure I can find (~30 bcm/y) describes the pair together. The same pattern shows up on Length: gem.wiki's own infobox gives each thread as '146 km each', and 146 x 2 = 292 -- exactly the figure stamped on BOTH rows. Belarusian TSO reporting conventions commonly total parallel threads into a single 'single-thread-equivalent' figure (btg.by's own activities page does this at the country level: 'общая протяженность газопроводов ... в однониточном исчислении' = 'total pipeline length ... in single-thread-equivalent terms'), which is a very plausible origin for a 292 = 146+146 mix-up landing on each individual thread row -- the same aggregate-vs-segment error class already documented for Kazakhstan. Separately, as a rough sanity check (not itself a citation): great-circle distance from Ivatsevichi, Belarus (~52.71N 25.34E) to Dolyna, Ukraine (~48.97N 23.98E) is roughly 425-430 km, which is hard to reconcile with EITHER 146 km or 292 km for a single continuous asset spanning that distance -- worth a routing/endpoint sanity check alongside the capacity/length fix, though I could not independently confirm the true route length and am not proposing a specific corrected number. I have not filled Capacity or Length with the current values' refs, since the sources I found do not actually support 29 bcm/y / 292 km as per-thread figures -- filling them would misrepresent what the sources say.

concerns.recommendation: Re-verify StartYear1: independent 2022 reporting places actual gas delivery into Melitopol at 2022-10-31, roughly 1.5 years before the recorded StartYear1=2024. Also re-examine ConstructionYear=2023/07: the sheet's own cited source (dan-news, verified live) describes a mid-life RE-LAY/upgrade of an existing, previously leaky pipe ('перекладка'), not the pipeline's original construction -- confirmed independently by the TASS/Wayback follow-up article, which quotes the same DNR official saying 'старые трубы были попросту дырявыми' (the old pipes were simply full of holes) before the 2023 work. Do not silently keep 2023/2024 as founding dates without settling whether they describe the ORIGINAL build (per neftegaz, ~2022) or a documented later capacity upgrade.
concerns.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2024, sourced to the now-dead TASS link: the TASS article recovered via Wayback (dated 2024-04-29) reports the EFFECTS of a 2023 upgrade being felt in winter 2023-24 (doubled pipeline pressure, 1.5x more gas volume, no more heating-season rationing) -- it does not claim the pipeline started operating in 2024. Independent, earlier reporting (neftegaz.ru, 2022-10-31, citing acting Zaporizhzhia governor Balitsky) states gas was already flowing into Melitopol on 2022-10-31, after Berdyansk received it on 2022-10-25 -- i.e. the pipeline (or at least the new Berdyansk-Melitopol section that reaches Melitopol) was delivering gas nearly a year and a half before the sheet's recorded StartYear1. ConstructionYear=2023/Month=7, sourced to dan-news (verified live, dated exactly 2023-07-27, matching the value): the DNR official's own quoted words are 'начаты работы по ПЕРЕКЛАДКЕ магистрального газопровода Таганрог-Мелитополь' -- 'relaying/re-laying', i.e. replacing pipe on an EXISTING corridor, not new construction from scratch. The TASS/Wayback follow-up (2024-04-29) confirms this was pipe replacement on old, deteriorated infrastructure ('старые трубы были попросту дырявыми'). Taken together, the two cited events (dan-news 2023-07, TASS 2024-04) appear to document a 2023 REHABILITATION/upgrade of an already-operating corridor, not the corridor's origin -- the corridor's actual first gas delivery to Melitopol traces independently to 2022-10-31 (neftegaz.ru).

status_changes.researcher_notes: The recorded Status='retired' (LastUpdated 2023-09-11) describes only the pipeline's 2009-2022 dormant period and is now stale: this line has been under active restoration/rebuild since mid-2022, well before the sheet's own last-update date. Timeline found: (1) Kommersant, 2022-07-13 — 'Ukrainian section' of the old Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk pipeline 'was not used after the 2009 gas conflict' but 'gas currently reaches Berdyansk from this direction' as of that date, and Russia's Energy Ministry/occupation governor Balitsky were actively working a restoration/extension plan (targeting completion in ~1.5 months, i.e. ~Sept 2022). (2) mariupol-news.ru, 2023-09-04 — reconstruction of the Mariupol GRS-1 station fed 'from the magistral gas pipeline Taganrog-Mariupol' is reported COMPLETE, with 150,000 m3/hour of new equipment, i.e. gas actively entering Mariupol's distribution network via this line as of that date. (3) United24 Media, 2025-07-24, citing the Ukrainian Center of Journalistic Investigations and 2024-dated video evidence — independently (this is the Ukrainian/non-Russian-origin corroborating leg) confirms Russia has been building pipelines on this exact Taganrog->Mariupol->Berdyansk axis as part of an ongoing land-corridor gas buildout, still described as under construction/expansion as recently as mid-2025. A DNR Minstroy order dated 2025-03-27 (approving planning documentation for 'capital repair of a linear object') looked like further corroboration but the domain (minstroy-dnr.ru) now 301-redirects to an unrelated site (gazetakursk.ru) — dead/repurposed, NOT cited, and the RBC 2022-10-25 report of DNR-sourced gas reaching Zaporizhzhia-Oblast settlements could not be verified (401, no Wayback snapshot) so is also not cited, though it is directionally consistent. Net read: 'retired' is wrong for the 2022-2025 period; the safest characterization given ongoing capital-repair/construction activity confirmed as recently as 2025 (rather than confirmed full-corridor commercial operation) is 'construction', even though the Mariupol-supplying sub-segment has apparently been delivering gas since ~2023. Tier held at medium rather than high per the country's occupied-territory rule (Russian-state/occupation-administration-linked sources — Kommersant, mariupol-news.ru/Donbassgaz — count as one origin; United24 is the second, independent, origin, but its corroboration is general/directional rather than a precise operational-status confirmation). Flagging for Update to decide between 'construction' (my recommendation, reflecting the still-incomplete Berdyansk/Melitopol extension) and 'operating' (defensible if the intent is to describe the Mariupol-supplying leg specifically, which has evidence of gas delivery since 2023) — either way, 'retired' should not stand.

The sheet's 'cancelled' is a real state, not an error -- Romanian press (economedia.ro headline, checked but returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, not cited) reported Transgaz DROPPED this project from its development plans in 2022 following the Russian invasion, and the project is absent from the intervening PDSNT editions (its own 'Modificari fata de planurile anterioare' comparison table in the new plan shows blank cells for the 2020/2022/2024 plan generations). BUT that changed after the sheet's 2025-05-29 update: Transgaz's shareholders gave PRELIMINARY approval on 21 July 2026 (98.29% of votes) to the updated PDSNT 2026-2030... 2035 plan, which REINSTATES this project as item 7.7 'Interconectare Romania - Ucraina pe directia Gherăiești - Siret', now in the 'Actualizare SPF' (updated pre-feasibility study) phase, target completion year 2032, investment estimate 450 million EUR (all confirmed directly in the plan PDF, section 7.7, and independently reported by stiripesurse.ro on 2026-07-22, which adds the shareholder-vote detail the plan PDF itself doesn't state -- treated as two distinct pieces of information even though both trace to Transgaz's corporate action). adevarul.ro (2026-05-03) independently corroborates the pre-vote version of the same plan naming 'interconectarea cu sistemul de transport din Ucraina (Gherăești-Siret)' among the planned 2026+ investments (verified via url_verifier, not counted toward tier given it covers the same underlying fact as the two cited sources). CAVEAT: all of this direct, dated evidence is for the ROMANIAN side of the interconnector (Transgaz's own project, section 7.7, covering the ~130 km Gheraesti-Siret pipe). I could not get independent confirmation that the UKRAINIAN side specifically (TSOUA's TRA-N-502, i.e. the physical asset this GEM row actually represents) has also been reinstated -- tsoua.com is Cloudflare-gated to every UA tried. The revival is inferred to extend to the Ukrainian spur because (a) ENTSOG tracks both halves under one project code (PRJ-G-121) and (b) the Transgaz plan explicitly states the point of the project IS to create new cross-border capacity with Ukraine at Siret ('Proiectul creeaza o noua capacitate transfrontaliera cu Ucraina in zona localitatii Siret') -- a Romanian-side line with no matching Ukrainian-side line would serve no purpose. Recommend Status='proposed' (early planning/pre-feasibility, matching the still-Pre-FID FIDStatus) rather than reverting to 'construction' or 'operating' -- nothing here suggests physical work has begun. StartYear1 proposed at 2032 to replace the stale 2025 figure (itself inherited from the abandoned 2018-2027/2021-2030 plan cycle); if ShelvedCancelledType is currently populated on this row it should be cleared along with the Status change. Flag this one for a human look before merging given the Ukrainian-side evidence gap -- a 'change' is proposed here per the >=2-source rule for the parent project, but a reviewer may reasonably want direct TSOUA confirmation before flipping this specific row.

[QC] independent=yes claimed on 1 surviving ref(s) from 1 publisher(s) -> no. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).

[QC] independent=yes claimed on 1 surviving ref(s) from 1 publisher(s) -> no. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).

Kharkivtransgaz's own 60-year history states the line was 'диаметром 1200 мм' with a twin-1200mm river crossing under the Krasnooskolske reservoir -- exact match to GEM. Verified by direct download + pdftotext -layout (the automated url_verifier screen false-negatives on this 17MB PDF, a documented failure mode of the tool itself for large PDFs). Both Novopskov and Shebelinka as start/end points are named explicitly and consistently in two independent origins: hvylya.net (2016 news analysis) and the Kharkivtransgaz corporate history (Wayback capture of a dead utg.ua PDF, confirmed by direct download). Both in Ukraine, matching GEM.

Both articles describe an in-service trunk line being taken offline temporarily for shelling repair (2015) or shelling damage (2022), each event framed as a disruption to a normally-operating asset (2015: ~2-day repair estimate, transit unaffected; 2022: dispatchers detecting a pressure anomaly on an operating system). Status is inferred from context per instructions, not required as a literal token match. No dated evidence of permanent decommissioning found.

Both sources call it газопровод (gas pipeline) throughout and describe natural-gas supply disruptions to downstream cities/gas-distribution stations as the consequence of the damage — fuel is unambiguously natural gas.

Both sources explicitly call it магистральный газопровод (МГП) — trunk/main gas pipeline, the standard Russian/Ukrainian term for a high-pressure transmission trunk as distinct from a gathering or feeder line (газопровод-отвод). The 2022 article's separate mention of a distinct газопровод-отвод (feeder) damaged in Kharkiv Oblast on 2022-03-02 shows the outlet uses the two terms deliberately, not interchangeably — the Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol line is squarely in the trunk/transmission category.

neftegaz.ru states the diameter directly and twice: 'Ду 1000' (диаметр условный / nominal diameter 1000mm), matching the sheet's Diameter=1000/mm exactly. Only one independent source found stating diameter specifically (biz.liga.net does not give a diameter figure) — tier medium, single strong source, not yet the 2-independent bar. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 1 surviving ref(s) from 1 publisher(s) -> no. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).

Both sources name the route by exactly this endpoint pair (Kramatorsk→Donetsk→Mariupol) and neftegaz.ru additionally pinpoints a mid-route damage location (Yasinovataysky district, between Krasnogorovka and Novokalinovo, near Ocheretino, NW of Donetsk city) — all inside Donetsk Oblast, consistent with the sheet's start/end oblast values. Mariupol is administratively part of Donetsk Oblast, matching EndState/Province. This confirms the corridor/route naming, not exact endpoint coordinates — no route geometry claim is made here.

Eustream's own press release documents commercial operation beginning 2 Sep 2014. No source found confirming continued operation past 2014-2020 specifically for this line (an ICIS piece from 30 Jun 2020 that does confirm active 2020 use of this exact crossing fails url_verifier as a stub/blocked page and cannot be cited). No evidence of closure or decommissioning was found anywhere, and per the country's standing rule, the 2025 end of Russian transit through Ukraine does not itself imply this reverse-flow import line (which never carried Russian transit gas -- it exists specifically to bring EU-sourced gas INTO Ukraine) went offline. Status=operating is retained on the strength of the commissioning source plus absence of any contrary reporting; flagged that a fresher confirmation would strengthen this. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).

Both Eustream (operator, 'transport to Ukraine 10 bcm of natural gas per year') and Kyiv Post/Interfax-Ukraine ('reverse supplies of natural gas from Slovakia to Ukraine') independently and explicitly describe this as a natural-gas pipeline. Two independent origins, both agreeing -- high tier.

Eustream's own press release is dated 02.09.2014 and states commercial operation began that day. Kyiv Post/Interfax-Ukraine (28 Apr 2014) independently forecasts launch in September 2014 reaching max capacity in October 2014 -- consistent with, and independently corroborating, StartYear1=2014. Two independent origins agreeing on the year -- high tier. (No month field forced; Eustream's release supports month=September if a StartMonth1 fill is later wanted.)

Eustream's own commercial-operation press release states the exact figure: '10 bcm of natural gas per year (27 mcm/day)' as full capacity, with 6.4 bcm/y (17.6 mcm/day) guaranteed minimum from Oct 2014 and firm service from Mar 2015. This is a single (though highly authoritative -- the pipeline's own operator) source; see the paired validity note on the superseded 8-9 bcm/y preliminary Eustream estimate reported by Kyiv Post, which traces to the same origin and so does not count as independent corroboration. Tier medium, not high. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).

GEM's own wiki page cites ICIS's 'Budince interconnector... single 700mm pipeline' article for this value, but that URL fails scripts/url_verifier.py (200 status, ~210-850 byte stub body -- a bot-block/paywall) every time it was tried, so per the hard requirement it cannot be cited here. No alternative source with an explicit diameter figure was located (Kyiv Post and both Eustream releases give capacity, not diameter). See the paired validity note for the ENTSOG size-class corroboration, which supports the 700mm order of magnitude but is not a citable text source for this value. Left UNRESOLVED rather than reusing an uncitable link.

Both sources name Vojany, Slovakia as the origin and Uzhhorod ('Uzhorod'), Ukraine as the destination -- exactly matching GEM's Start/EndLocation and Start/EndCountryOrArea. Two independent sources agreeing -- high tier. The cross-border split (Slovakia->Ukraine) is correctly recorded, consistent with this being a genuine interconnector, not an internal Ukrainian line.

Eustream's 1-Jan-2025 release (Slovak TSO, official) states 'the transmission of natural gas continues at all interconnection points' at this exact border point even as the Russia-transit forward flow stopped -- direct confirmation the asset is in service, not retired. EP Power Europe (unrelated Czech energy group) independently describes the Veľké Kapušany compressor station in the present tense as 'the biggest compressor station in the EU', a live description of currently-operating infrastructure at the Ukraine entry/exit point. Two independent, non-GEM origins.
Both sources describe this crossing explicitly as natural-gas transmission infrastructure (a 'Gas Transmission' business line / 'zemný plyn' [natural gas] flow). No ambiguity.

Eustream's 2014 release places the reverse-flow inauguration event 'at the Compressor Station in Veľké Kapušany' as the Slovak-side node of the 'Vojany-Uzhorod' (i.e. Uzhhorod-side) connection; EP Power Europe independently confirms Veľké Kapušany is the entry/exit point 'to/from the natural gas transmission network in Ukraine', close to the Ukrainian-Slovak border. Both endpoints (Uzhhorod, Ukraine / Veľké Kapušany, Slovakia) corroborated by two independent, non-GEM sources.

Both sources treat the pipeline as a live, in-service transmission asset undergoing active maintenance/reconstruction (the whole point of a reconstruction project is to keep an operating line safe) rather than a retired one. I found no dated evidence that the Du700 pipe has been decommissioned since; per the country-scope rule I am not inferring a status change from the end of Russian transit (irrelevant to this domestic Donbas-supply line) or from the war generally (no line-specific damage/closure report found) — tier medium rather than high because neither source is a direct 2026 'still operating today' statement, just the most recent dated evidence available plus the absence of any contrary report. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).
Both sources describe this as a 'газопровід' (gas pipeline) carrying natural gas from the Shebelynka gas field; Fuel=Gas is correct.

Ukrainian Wikipedia and TSOUA's own (Wayback-captured) project page independently state the pipeline was built/commissioned in 1969; TSOUA's text is highly specific ('побудований у 1969 р.', built in 1969) matching GEM's StartYear1=1969 exactly.

Neither source states exactly '70.00 km' — Ukrainian Wikipedia and a ProZorro tender title both say '67 km' (corridor km1.1 to km68.0), and TSOUA's own project text extends the reconstruction scope to km68.6. 70.00km is close to, but not an exact match for, this ~67-68.6km cluster (a ~3-4% gap, i.e. below the >10% material-conflict threshold). Tier medium (not high) to reflect that the sources corroborate the pipeline's approximate length and corridor extent rather than exactly the stated 70.00km figure; see the spec caveat in validity[] for the full reasoning. Not proposing a value change. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).

700mm (Du700) as-built diameter is confirmed by both sources. See the spec caveat in validity[]: this is the historically correct and best-currently-supported figure, but TSOUA's own document describes an active, partially-completed plan to replace it with Du500 along most of the corridor and eventually dismantle the Du700 pipe — no evidence found that this has been completed as of 2026, so 700mm stands.
Both independent sources describe this as a газопровід (gas pipeline) carrying Shebelynka field gas to Donbas consumers.
Both sources explicitly describe the reconstruction as replacing Du700 with Du500 (заміна Ду 700 на Ду 500) — matches GEM's 500.00 mm exactly for the new pipe P3382 is meant to represent.

iSANS's Feb 2023 Belarusian energy-security report states: '«Ивацевичи — Долина» диаметром 1220 мм (около 30 млрд куб. м. в год)' — 'Ivatsevichi-Dolina, diameter 1220mm (about 30 billion m3/year)'. This is the COMBINED capacity of the twin-thread system (both P3484 and P5938 together), and it closely matches the sheet's per-row figure of 29 bcm/y (29 vs ~30, within normal rounding for a secondary source). NOTE for a human reviewer: it is not fully clear whether GEM's convention on this row is meant to record the single-thread capacity or the whole-corridor capacity duplicated onto both parallel rows — if the latter, summing P3484+P5938 would overstate true throughput roughly 2x, the same shape as the Length concern filed separately. I am citing this source because it corroborates the VALUE as printed (29≈30), not because it resolves the per-thread-vs-system question; url_verifier cannot parse PDF text directly (it checked HTTP 200 only), so I manually confirmed the '1220 мм' / '30 млрд куб. м.' text via pdftotext -layout on the downloaded PDF. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 1 surviving ref(s) from 1 publisher(s) -> no. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).

Two independent sources corroborate the Ivatsevichy(Belarus)->Dolyna(Ukraine) corridor: iSANS 2023 ('Украина и Беларусь связаны ... газопроводом «Ивацевичи — Долина»' — Ukraine and Belarus are connected by the Ivatsevichi-Dolina pipeline) and East European Gas Analysis's Belarus pipeline scheme (eegas.com/belarus1.htm: 'Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi, 3 x 1220mm' feeding into 'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina, 2 x 1220mm', consistent with Ivatsevichy as the Belarusian junction point and Dolyna as the Ukrainian terminus/hub). Both verified live via url_verifier (eegas directly; isans PDF confirmed via pdftotext since url_verifier only checks HTTP 200 on PDFs).

Moldovatransgaz lists this line among its 8 currently-operated trunk pipelines, and a second Moldovatransgaz release documents active 2020-2021 tie-in/reconstruction work on it, i.e. the asset is in service and being actively maintained, not abandoned. No dated evidence of any outage/mothballing was found, so 'operating' stands; medium tier because neither source is dated to the present (2026) explicitly, only continuity in the absence of contrary evidence.
Explicitly and repeatedly described as a 'газопровод' (gas pipeline) transporting natural gas ('природный газ').
Called a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline) built to supply end consumers of the country — a transmission trunk, not a gathering/process/feeder line.

Exact match to Moldovatransgaz's current published capacity (1.3 billion m3/year). See the companion validity entry (concern_type=spec) — a second, affiliated company source gives a materially lower 1966 original design figure (570 million m3/y); tier held at medium rather than high because of that unresolved conflict, even though GEM's own number is the one that matches the current operator source.
Two independent company sources (current operator Moldovatransgaz + parent Moldovagaz's separate historical article) both state 44 km exactly.
Both sources state Ду530 / 530 mm exactly — no unit-conversion round-trip artifact (unlike P1465/P1773 elsewhere in this country's roster).

The pipeline's own name and description tie it to the Odesa junction with Ukraine's gas transmission system, which is the gas-supply origin point feeding into Moldova on this line. Tier medium: this is a reasonable inference from the source's description of the pipeline's Ukrainian-side connection, not a source using the literal field label 'FuelSource'.
The pipeline's name and both sources confirm the Odesa (Ukraine) → Chisinau (Moldova) endpoints.

Could not independently confirm 1981 as Thread II's start year. gem.wiki's own infobox differentiates Thread I=1976 / Thread II=1981 (read for leads only, not citable), but its footnotes for that claim are a 2001 Finmarket article and the 2023 iSANS report, neither of which I could confirm actually states a construction year for this specific thread. A Belarusian gasification-history search surfaced a near-miss: mogilev.gas.by's museum timeline dates the SECOND thread of 'Kobrin-Brest' (a different, nearby pipeline) to 1976 -- not Ivatsevichi-Kobryn-Dolyna. Leaving unresolved rather than fabricating support for a number I could not verify.

Plausible (Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi, which physically feeds this line at Ivatsevichi, does carry West Siberian/Urengoy-origin gas), but I found no source that names Urengoy specifically as the gas source for the Ivatsevichi-Dolina leg itself. Note this corridor's much older Soviet-era predecessor (Dashava-Ivatsevichi-Minsk, per ru.wikipedia's Belarus GTS article) historically ran the OPPOSITE direction, carrying western-Ukrainian (Dashava-area) gas north into Belarus -- so the modern flow direction/source is not something I would assume without a source. Leaving unresolved.

Both sources explicitly name the pipeline as connecting Ivatsevichi (Belarus) and Dolina (Ukraine): eegas.com lists 'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina, 2 x 1220 mm'; the archived btg.by activities page lists 'двухниточный магистральный газотрубопровод «Ивацевичи — Долина»' among the pipelines carrying Russian transit gas onward into Ukraine. Two independent origins agreeing on both endpoints -> high.

TASS/Wayback names the pipeline 'Таганрог-Мелитополь' explicitly and states it supplies Zaporizhzhia ('Запорожье'), matching EndState/Province=Zaporizhzhia Oblast and EndLocation=Melitopol. DAN independently confirms the same pipeline name and that it passes through DNR territory en route (consistent with a Taganrog, Russia origin). Taganrog itself being in Rostov Oblast is undisputed public geography, not separately sourced. Tier medium and independent=false per the country-scope rule: both citing sources are Russian state/occupation-linked outlets reporting the same DNR official's statements, i.e. one origin bucket, not two independent ones -- flagging explicitly rather than claiming high confidence. [QC] tier medium -> high (one validated ref is sufficient, rule 4).
